fullText:
Firmware updates have been the weakest link for a decade with smart homes. Every sensor, light bulb, and smart lock in your house runs software that should be updated regularly. This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Device updates from one place

Homey’s new Device Updates feature lets you update Matter, Z-Wave, and Zigbee devices directly from the Homey Mobile App or Web App. You can update a Matter light, install a security patch for a Z-Wave lock, or improve a Zigbee sensor’s reliability, all without ever opening a manufacturer’s app. You start the update, and Homey handles the rest, including delivery, progress tracking, and a notification when it’s done. Updates are available in More > Settings > Device Updates or in each device’s Maintenance settings.

For Z-Wave and Zigbee gear, updates are delivered via their respective Homey apps, so availability depends on the developer and manufacturer. The launch list of supported vendors is already pretty solid: IKEA, Aeotec, INNR, Niko, Inovelli, Zooz, frient, ThirdReality, EcoDim, HeatIt, Namron, amina, CTM Lyng, and Nous have added support, with more to come soon.

“Device firmware rarely gets updated because the process is cumbersome,” said Stefan Witkamp, CEO at Athom. “By handling device updates inside Homey, we make it practical for both users and developers. That makes the whole smart home more dependable.”

The Matter part is the real story

For Matter devices, Homey doesn’t rely on manufacturer apps at all, and manufacturers don’t need to update their Homey app for it to work. Homey checks the Connectivity Standards Alliance’s Distributed Compliance Ledger for available Matter firmware updates. The DCL provides the firmware version, download URL, file size, checksum, and applicability information. Homey then retrieves the firmware from the manufacturer-provided URL and delivers it to the device using Matter’s standardized OTA update mechanism.

The DCL is basically a trusted public registry for Matter products, run by the same organization that certifies them and is behind the Matter standard itself. Manufacturers publish firmware update metadata to the Matter Distributed Compliance Ledger, allowing Homey to discover and grab the available updates.

This means that the update path for Matter devices isn’t tied to any one company’s app or cloud service. It’s part of the actual Matter standard itself, verified by the certification body, and any Matter controller could implement it.

If you don’t see an update you expect, it’s usually because the device’s Homey app doesn’t offer it yet, or the manufacturer hasn’t published one. Device Updates is available on Homey Cloud, Homey Pro (2023 through 2026), Homey Pro mini, and Homey Self-Hosted Server, and requires v13.2.0 or later of the Homey Mobile App.

Eve devices now work with Homey, thanks to Matter

Speaking of Matter doing what it promised, there’s a second piece of Homey news worth covering. With Homey Pro and Homey Pro mini acting as Matter Controllers and Thread Border Routers, Matter-enabled Eve devices now work with Homey. That covers favorites I’ve written about plenty in this column: Eve Energy, Eve Door & Window, Eve Motion, Eve Thermo, Eve Weather, Eve MotionBlinds, and more.

Eve has always been one of the most trusted and privacy-focused brands in the smart home (with deep Apple Home integration), with no cloud service, no registration, and no tracking. If you’re running Eve gear in Apple Home today, nothing changes. What’s changed is that the same Thread and Matter foundation that made Eve great in Apple Home now makes it portable across other platforms, and that flexibility is exactly the point of the Matter standard. It’s a protocol vs a platform.

Wrap up

For years, the smart home industry has promised interoperability and delivered walled gardens with extra steps. Simply working with the big 3-4 major platforms isn’t enough. This Homey news is what the long-term benefits of Matter are proving to bring: firmware updates going through the standard body itself.

Matter has taken plenty of criticism for moving slowly, but features like this are why it matters.

This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of.

title: Apple Music opens new live music venue in London

fullText:
Apple is opening a new live music venue in Battersea Power Station, London. The new location is called Apple Music Hall, and even has its own website where fans can sign up to get alerted when the first tickets are available. 

The 600-person capacity venue will be the stage for intimate one-show-only concerts by artists, which will also be live-streamed for all Apple Music subscribers to enjoy.

The hall features a 38-foot wide stage, a 48-speaker surround sound system for an immersive Spatial Audio experience, and can support more than 16 broadcast cameras as well as iPhone video capture.

Apple says an artist can do a single intimate performance for fans, and immediately have a broadcast-ready mix, Spatial Audio recording, and multi-angle video of the event when they are done. Apple Music Hall is opening on September 28, although the first acts have not yet been announced.

Alongside this news, Apple also announced that it Is opening new radio station studios at Battersea, with all the London-based Apple Music Radio hosts now broadcasting from there.

title: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking powers Gemini Live, Gmail, & Keep
snippet: Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.”

Following the launch of 3.1 Flash Live in March, the new models aim to “make conversing with AI feel more intuitive and intelligent.” 

As the name suggests, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking offers “increased intelligence and multi-step reasoning.” It’s meant for high-complexity tasks like the recently launched Gmail Live (conversational search), Docs Live (draft generation and editing), and Keep Live (note creation). The model is also beginning to roll out to Gemini Live today.

3.8 Live Extended Thinking “reasons and speaks simultaneously.”

	

It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow — using early verbal cues like “Let me check that…” to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress.

In terms of benchmarks: 

“…the #1 overall spot on Artificial Analysis’ Speech to Speech Quality Index (82.6)”

“…leads in agentic task completion with 68.6% on τ-Voice”

“…35.1% on Sierra’s τ-Voice-banking benchmark”

“…strong reasoning capabilities, scoring 97.7% on Big Bench Audio, while maintaining a highly competitive price point compared to other frontier models.”

Meanwhile, the Gemini 3.8 Live base model offers “conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding.” The model can process “visual inputs in near real-time,” with tools and API calls executing in the background while the conversation continues. 

Users can expect the model to “acknowledge requests and keep chatting while tasks finish in the background.” Additionally, it can detect and transition between 97 supported languages mid-conversation. 

It’s “built for scale and cost efficiency” with a “second place in the Speech Agent Arena.” Gemini 3.8 Live will power AI Mode’s Search Live experience.

snippet: Amazon plans to spend $20 million on water conservation projects along the Colorado River, a crucial but dwindling water supply for 40 million people in the Western US. fullText:
Amazon plans to spend $20 million on water conservation projects along the Colorado River, a crucial but dwindling water supply for 40 million people in the Western US.

The initiative comes as Amazon and other tech companies face mounting scrutiny over how much water their data centers use. Amazon has a goal of becoming water positive — replenishing more water than it uses — by the end of the decade. It recently disclosed some information about its water use, but we still have an incomplete picture of the company’s impact as a whole.

Amazon announced the launch of a Colorado River Basin Collaborative today, with a mission to “create one of the biggest corporate water conservation efforts for a single U.S. watershed.” It expects to raise $100 million over two years — including the $20 million investment from its own coffers — for water conservation efforts.

The Colorado River brings water to 40 million people

Stretching 1,400 miles, the Colorado River brings water to 40 million people across seven states in the Western US and and two states in Mexico. The waterway has faced “unprecedented” drought over the last 26 years, according to the US Bureau of Reclamation. Decades of overuse on top of human-caused climate change have exacerbated the problem. To cope, the US Department of the Interior finalized a plan in August imposing steep water cuts on Arizona, Nevada, and California.

As the first stop for most goods the US imports from Asia, California is home to more Amazon warehouses than any other state. In Orange County, California, Amazon pledged $2.2 million over the next three years to help detect and patch up leaks. That effort is ultimately supposed to conserve 189 million gallons of water each year, according to Amazon.

As part of the newly announced collaborative, other companies can contract independently with conservation projects they choose. The United Nations-backed Water Resilience Coalition will vet projects. Amazon is also joining the Water Resilience Coalition, which includes Microsoft, Meta, and other brands across a range of sectors.

Tech companies are facing waves of resistance against new AI data centers. AI was estimated to use between 312.5 billion and 764.6 billion liters of water in 2025, according to one estimate, about as much water as people consume globally in water bottles. In Arizona, Colorado River water cuts are expected to raise utility rates, and some residents fear data centers could make things worse.

In June, Amazon disclosed that its data centers used 2.5 billion gallons of water globally in 2025, including those it owns, leases, or shares. Data centers Amazon owns and operates directly reduced their water consumption by 2 percent in 2025 compared to the year prior, according to the company. It attributes gains to a 52 percent improvement in water efficiency since 2021. The company says it uses 0.12 liters of water per kilowatt-hour of electricity, claiming that’s about seven times more efficient than the industry average for data centers.

Amazon’s annual sustainability report shares water use per unit of power (l/kwh) for its data centers since 2021, but not the company’s total water use over that time period. Sustainability experts and environmental advocates caution against assessing a company’s sustainability by efficiency measurements alone. The more efficient a technology becomes, the more resources it might ultimately consume as companies start using it more, according to an economic concept called Jevons paradox. That makes it important to track how much water a company is using overall, as well as how much it needs in each place it operates during demand peaks when supply is most limited.

For comparison, Microsoft’s latest sustainability report discloses its data centers’ total water use since 2020, while Google’s report shares water use for global operations since 2021 with a breakdown by location. All three tech giants have had to abandon data center projects after facing community opposition, Reuters reports. Unlike other tech companies, Amazon’s warehouses also have a massive physical footprint that isn’t reflected in the company’s data center disclosures.

A Guardian investigation in 2025 alleges that Amazon obscured how much water the company uses by deciding not to account for how much it takes to generate electricity, considered a “secondary” water use. Concerned about “reputational risk,” executives decided to only address “primary” water use at its facilities when calculating progress toward sustainability goals. The numbers Amazon recently shared about its data center water use also exclude water consumption stemming from electricity generation.

While data centers often use water for cooling systems, a majority of a data center’s water footprint stems from this “secondary use.” Power plants need water to cool equipment and turn turbines using steam, and in 2021, Amazon used 10.5 billion gallons (39.7 billion liters) of water in 2021, according to the Guardian report citing an internal leaked document. That’s about as much as 95,000 US households consume.

In an email to The Verge, Amazon spokesperson Margaret Callahan says the Guardian report “relied on cherry-picked data from an outdated document that misrepresents our water strategy — making the conclusions fundamentally wrong and misleading” and that a “document’s existence doesn’t guarantee its accuracy or finality.”

Callahan didn’t provide more data on how much water Amazon has used in total over the years. She pointed out that the company is 75 percent toward its goal of becoming water positive, returning 3 gallons for every 4 that it used last year.

In its announcement today, Kara Hurst, chief sustainability officer at Amazon, compares the new Colorado River initiative to the company’s previous climate targets.

”Through the Climate Pledge, we’ve seen what happens when companies tackle a problem together: progress accelerates. We’re bringing that same model to the Colorado River because water and climate are deeply connected,” Hurst says.

Amazon’s carbon footprint, however, grew 16 percent in 2025 — a trend happening across the tech industry as companies race to make advances in AI.

title: Apple Music in iOS 27: Five new features just added for iPhone
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below.

#1: Landscape mode

iOS 27 adds support for landscape layouts to many system apps, including Apple Music. The feature will be especially nice on iPhone Duo, but other iPhone models benefit too.

With landscape mode, you can view music artwork alongside playback controls just like in portrait orientation. 

More important to me though, lyrics are now available side-by-side with artwork. I’ve found this a great way to enjoy music while my iPhone is docked on a desk or kitchen charger.

#2: AutoMix improvements

AutoMix debuted last year in iOS 26, but Apple has upgraded and expanded it this year in iOS 27.

Per Apple’s press release:

AutoMix has added a whole new layer of energy and excitement to the experience with even better transitions that feel more immersive and engaging for listeners. AutoMix will also be available on Apple Music in tvOS and on HomePod.

Like my colleague Chance, I’ve definitely found AutoMix transitions improved this year. In iOS 26 I sometimes loved the feature and other times found it frustrating. In iOS 27 so far it’s been almost entirely a positive for me.

#3: New design for artist pages

Artist pages get a refreshed look in iOS 27, with a design that takes inspiration from iOS 26.4’s updates for albums and playlists.

Like albums, artist pages now have fullscreen color backgrounds that complement their header image. You can see several examples above.

Artist pages also make key controls more convenient to access, and their featured music title is more prominently displayed than before.

#4: Friends playlist

Apple’s roster of weekly-updated ‘Made for You’ playlists expands in iOS 27 with a new Friends playlist. Per Apple’s description:

The best of what your friends are listening to. Updated every Thursday.

The playlist is a convenient new way to get a taste of your friends’ current favorites. Each track shows you which friend is listening to it too.

iOS 27 introduces an extra-large widget size for the first time, and Apple Music takes advantage of it more than any other app.

Apple Music has three new extra-large widgets: 

Recently Played

Recommendations

Top Charts

These widgets can be added to your Home Screen or Today view, offering more flexibility in personalizing your iPhone.

title: Clicks Communicator lands in December with 12GB RAM, two months of free data
snippet: Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans. more…
fullText:
Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans.

When the company announced the Clicks Communicator back at CES this year, it was primarily pitched as a secondary device meant to pair with your main smartphone. It seems like the team has heard from its potential customers that some might be satisfied with this being their main smartphone, which has prompted a handful of changes to improve the overall experience.

By far, the biggest upgrade is a move from 8GB to 12GB of RAM, something I’ll be calling a “reverse Pixel 11 Pro” situation. While other smartphone makers are doing whatever they can to reduce RAM — while increasing prices along the way — Clicks is adding additional memory to the device to better futureproof the phone. Its upgrade policy isn’t quite on par with Google or Samsung, but three promised OS upgrades and five years of security updates will, at the very least, pull your Communicator through to around 2032. Clicks has also moved its launch platform to Android 17 out of the box and bumped its battery capacity up to 4,350mAh. 

On the accessory side, Clicks and Dbrand are bringing the latter’s new MNML cases to the device, along with its Prism screen protector that includes a self-aligning tray — is there any other way? Clicks will also continue to offer its bumper Ring case for those looking for a more minimal approach to protection. Dbrand’s case and screen protector will run you $39 and $35, respectively, while the Ring bumper case is $49. Additional Charging Covers, allowing you to switch up your phone’s design, will also be available for $50 or $80, depending on material.

	

Finally, Clicks is launching both a protection plan and eSIM options for its users. title: iPhone 18 Pro Face ID bug causing system to crash and reboot for some users
snippet: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar. It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 27. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt. more…
fullText:
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max introduces a new smaller Face ID system, with the Infrared camera now hidden behind the screen, near where the time is shown in the status bar.

It appears there may be a software glitch with that component in the shipping release of iOS 27. A number of reports from 18 Pro owners indicate that their device freezes and reboots after a failed Face ID attempt.

9to5Mac has reproduced the bug on at least one European iPhone 18 Pro model. The scope of the problem is unclear, as it does not seem to affect everyone. 

The issue appears to occur when using Face ID to unlock a protected app, like the Passwords app, private tabs in Safari, or other apps the user has chosen to lock behind biometric protection. It does not seem to trigger directly from the lock screen.

To try and reproduce for yourself, on an 18 Pro, when the device presents a Face ID challenge, cover your face with your hand to simulate an authentication failure on the first try. Then, tap the “Try Face ID Again” button in the alert that appears. If you are afflicted by the bug, the phone will lock up and stop responding to all touch input. After a few seconds, the phone panics and reboots back to the lock screen. 

In the Reddit thread of complaining users, one person says they contacted Apple support who apparently recommended a hardware swap. In our experience, this is probably a misdiagnosis and the problem will be fixable by a software update. 

There’s also a similar iOS 27 bug that can trigger system reboots on any iPhone model, which we also expect to be fixed by a forthcoming software patch.

We have reached out to Apple for comment on the matter and will let you know if we hear back.

title: iPhone 20 Pro Rumor Hints at Apple’s Wildest All-Glass Redesign
snippet: Next year’s models could have the biggest screens in iPhone history.
fullText:
Hope there’s plenty of room in your pockets. Apple’s rumored iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max could have the largest displays in iPhone history alongside a quad-curved, nearly all-glass exterior.

Digital Chat Station, a prominent anonymous tech insider on the Chinese social media platform Weibo and a reliable source of Apple news in the past, posted over the weekend that the iPhone 20 Pro screen would be 6.41 inches and the Pro Max 6.96 inches, measured diagonally. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which hit stores last Friday, measure 6.27 inches and 6.86 inches (Apple rounds up to 6.3 inches and 6.9 inches). The iPhone Duo, Apple’s long-awaited first foldable phone, which reaches stores on Oct. 23, has a diagonal 7.6-inch inner display when open.

A representative for Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

CNET Senior Reporter Abrar Al-Heeti said that larger screens are great for watching videos and working on the go, but bigger displays also mean higher costs for consumers, serving as an “excuse for companies to charge you more.” 

“Along with the commemorative angle of the iPhone’s 20th anniversary, it’s likely Apple could use design elements like a bigger screen and an all-glass design to hike prices,” Al-Heeti said. 

More glass, smaller Dynamic Island

Digital Chat Station backed Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman’s August report that the exterior of the new flagship phones would be nearly all glass in what’s called a quad-curved design. That means the glass will wrap around all four sides of the phone, making it look as if there is no bezel.

In his report last month, Gurman said that the glass on the front and back of the phones would “curve into the sides of the devices, with a metal band in the middle.”

The exteriors of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are made of aluminum and ceramic glass.

The iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max will also have a smaller Dynamic Island and a tiny punch-hole selfie cutout on the front, according to Digital Chat Station.

The Dynamic Island is the capsule-shaped region at the top of the front screen that houses the selfie camera and which also expands and contracts to display notifications, system alerts and background activities.

The iPhone 20 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch in September 2027 as the next iteration in the series. Apple is widely expected to skip over the iPhone 19 name and jump straight to iPhone 20 next year, marking the 20th anniversary of the first iPhone launch in 2007.

											Ever since being admittedly fascinated by the Cambridge coffee webcam from the 1990s, I've written about VPNs, the NFL, smartphones, living wages, over/unders and everything in between.

title: iPadOS 27.2 adds convenient new feature from the Mac
snippet: iPadOS 27.2 arrived in beta this week, and beyond adding the redesigned Health app, Apple has also brought over a recent Mac feature: a Siri popup when text is selected. more…
fullText:
iPadOS 27.2 arrived in beta this week, and beyond adding the redesigned Health app, Apple has also brought over a recent Mac feature: a Siri popup when text is selected.

Siri AI is the tentpole addition to iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and companion releases. And as such, Apple offers lots of ways to access the new, supercharged assistant.

On iPad you can invoke Siri via a “Siri” or “Hey Siri” voice prompt, pull down from the top of the screen, use the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or my personal favorite: use CMD + Space to open Spotlight and ask Siri a question from there.

But iPadOS 27.2 adds yet another option that’s borrowed directly from the Mac.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, in many situations when you select some text, a small Siri icon appears in the top-left corner of the selection. When you hover over the icon with your cursor, it expands to offer an ‘Ask Siri’ text box.

This wasn’t available in iPadOS 27. But now, if you have a trackpad connected to your iPad, that same behavior is available in iPadOS 27.2.

As seen in the images above, the new Siri icon starts out small and stays out of the way, but it’s very convenient to just hover over it to make the ‘Ask Siri’ box appear.

If you don’t have a trackpad attached, selecting text will still reveal the full edit menu where you can tap to open Siri. But it’s a more smooth and seamless experience with a trackpad.

macOS is full of small productivity-focused features like this that speed up everyday interactions, yet are missing from iPadOS. So it’s exciting to see such a recent Mac feature be brought over to the iPad.

What do you think of the new Siri popup in iPadOS 27.2? Let us know in the comments.

In this day and age, gas prices fluctuate quite a lot. If you want to have a better idea of how things are flowing, GasPulse is a great tool – giving you trends, historical prices, and an outlook to follow on your iPhone.

Top features

Using the weekly averages published by the Energy Information Administration, GasPulse shows you prices for each state or region. It’s not an app that’ll show you the cheapest gas station, but it shows you the trends with charts and a nice interface. It also has up to five years of historical prices.

Beyond that, it also offers an Outlook feature that gives you an idea of what to expect in the future. These are estimates, but it gives you a little bit of insight on whether or not things will go up or down. GasPulse also offers state-by-state comparisons, allowing you to see how things compare around you.

If you want price alerts, GasPulse also offers them for free for up to 6 areas, though it relies on iOS background refresh.

Lastly, GasPulse offers home screen and lock screen widgets, allowing you to keep an eye on things without opening the app. There’s also Siri support.

Download the app

GasPulse is available for free on the App Store for iPhone users running iOS 18 and later. There’s no requirement for a subscription, and it’s ad-free.

title: iOS 27.2 reveals new features coming to Apple Music, CarPlay, more
snippet: iOS 27.2 beta 2 arrived today, and so far seems to have minimal user-facing changes. But code for iOS 27.2’s beta releases points to new features in the works for Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, and more. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 beta 2 arrived today, and so far seems to have minimal user-facing changes. But code for iOS 27.2’s beta releases points to new features in the works for Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, and more.

Whenever Apple releases new beta software, we tend to discover changes in two ways: through user-facing features active in the software, as well as underlying code changes that point to forthcoming changes.

With iOS 27.2, there were a variety of new features available for testing from day one, like the all-new Health app, user profiles in Apple TV, Siri AI expansions, and more.

But users skilled at examining the underlying code found even more changes in the works. 

For example, X user pdfu discovered that Apple Music will soon add live countdowns for new album releases.

Another discovery by pdfu in iOS 27.2 beta code involves the Shortcuts app.

Shortcuts’ new ‘Describe a Shortcut’ feature looks like it will soon gain support for including actions from third-party apps.

Describe a Shortcut could soon support actions from third-party developers.

Currently, the feature only supports Apple-developed actions. With a new feature flag in iOS 27.2 and macOS 27.2, the model can now choose actions from third-party apps.

title: CarPlay just got better, here’s everything new in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 has arrived, and with it a handful of improvements for CarPlay. Here’s everything new for CarPlay in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 has arrived, and with it a handful of improvements for CarPlay. Here’s everything new for CarPlay in iOS 27.

Siri AI and new Siri app

Apple’s Siri overhaul is the tentpole addition to iOS 27. And the new ‘Siri AI’ capabilities on the iPhone are available in CarPlay too if you have a compatible iPhone.

Siri AI offers a new design that’s more like the pre-iOS 18 look, but with less color. It appears as a glowing orb at the bottom-center of the screen.

Siri in CarPlay is now much better at answering questions of any kind, similar to ChatGPT and Google Gemini. In my testing, it’s also able to retain the context of your current conversation better than ever before. Here are 100+ examples of what Siri AI can do.

In a nice touch, conversations you have in CarPlay are automatically synced to the Siri app on iPhone. You can browse the full Siri history in the app, and there’s a car icon marking conversations you had via CarPlay.

Video app support

Apple added video in the car with iOS 26, but it was limited to AirPlay streaming. But with iOS 27 developers can now make dedicated video apps for CarPlay, so that users can browse videos right on their CarPlay display.

From Apple’s WWDC video that’s targeted toward developers:

With iOS 27 you can create apps to browse and play videos in new cars that support the video in car feature. If your app supports AirPlay video streaming, no changes are needed. People can already watch videos from your app on their CarPlay display when they aren’t driving. To do so, they simply select the car’s display when playing the video on iPhone. Now you can take it to the next level and let people browse their favorite videos from iPhone right on their CarPlay display.

Automakers need to sign on to support the feature, so unfortunately it won’t be available automatically in every car.

New design updates and wallpapers

iOS 27 has a handful of design-related updates for CarPlay too. 

As seen above, media apps feature a new MiniPlayer in CarPlay. Available in the top-right corner of the app, the MiniPlayer provides artwork and player controls—a nice upgrade with more utility than the previous waveform icon offered.

You can now do audio scrubbing on the Now Playing screen when listening to music, audiobooks, or podcasts. There’s a larger progress indicator that’s similar to the iPhone design, making it easy to grab and drag.

App icons have been refreshed with updated Liquid Glass designs in iOS 27, and those new icons extend to CarPlay.

Finally, there are new CarPlay wallpapers available now that resemble what’s included across iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate.

Which new CarPlay features in iOS 27 are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google fully details Googlebooks: $899+, October launch, & more
snippet: Following the May preview, Google today fully announced Googlebooks ahead of the consumer launch in October. more…
fullText:
Following the May preview, Google today fully announced Googlebooks ahead of the consumer launch in October.

Googlebook OS hands-on: It’s Android, stupid

Software

Google’s main pitch is that Googlebooks should be the laptop of choice for those with Android phones:

Today, we often switch between starting tasks on our phones and finishing them on our laptops. To make that experience better for Android users, we teamed up with the best laptop makers in the industry to deliver top-tier hardware alongside Google’s software experience that connects effortlessly with your phone.

Following phones and watches, Material 3 Expressive is coming to desktops. Quick Settings and notifications, which are nearly identical in design to what you’d find on Pixel, can be found in the top-right corner, while you have the time and date at the left. The bottom dock is center-aligned with the ‘G’ opening your app drawer. 

	

Upon signing in to a Googlebook, your Android phone’s settings, saved passwords, Wi-Fi, and messages will appear. Cross-device continuity includes Android 17’s “Continue On” capability and Cast My Apps if you don’t want to install the Android application on your laptop.

Additionally, Google touts a first-class Files app that can show what documents and photos are available on your phone. One good use of on-device AI is automatically generating file descriptions that aid search.

Gemini Intelligence is led by Magic Pointer and the wiggle gesture to bring up Gemini and enter a prompt, like adding dates to your Calendar. There’s also Rambler, like on the Pixel 11 series, to dictate a stream of consciousness, while Create My Widget is billed as letting you “customize your desktop by describing what you need in plain language.”

You get a “desktop-class” Chrome browser with support for extensions, the Gemini side panel, vertical tabs, and more. Most features found on Mac and Windows are available here.

The application story is a combination of Android and the web, with Google noting how 70% of time spent on laptops is in a browser. The company ultimately thinks it is up to developers to choose whether an Android app or the web is better for their application. There is a growing number of desktop-class Android apps, and the Play Store will highlight them with a new badge. 

On the gaming front, 20,000 mobile and PC titles will run on Googlebooks. They are optimized for keyboard, mouse, and touchscreen, with Google’s existing Play Games Level Up program resulting in monthly title launches. For everything else, Google offers a year of Nvidia GeForce Now.

For developers, Google very notably created an Antigravity app for Googlebooks that offers a native UI and interacts with the Linux environment. You can also install the Linux version of Antigravity if you wish, along with Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex. For Android app development, Antigravity allows you to deploy directly to the Googlebook.

Under the hood, Google is integrating the multi-window performance and full browser capabilities of ChromeOS with a native Android stack that offers power and battery efficiency.

On the security front, Google touts the same security architecture as ChromeOS. There’s a Google Titan security chip and on-device malware detection. Additionally, a Level 5 security-certified hypervisor powered by pKVM isolation allows for the isolated Linux environment with full terminal access. This lets you “safely run any Linux developer tools, pull code repositories, access networks and the ports, or execute autonomous agents.”

Googlebooks get 10 years of automatic updates with quarterly feature drops similar to Pixel.

Hardware

On the hardware front, there are five flagship Googlebooks at launch, with Google mandating several key specs across the lineup. All devices are powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 or Snapdragon X Elite with NPUs (40+ TOPS). As such, Googlebook OS is optimized for ARM and x86, with MediaTek-powered devices coming in the future.

There’s a baseline of 16 GB of RAM with 32 GB variants available. All have a touchscreen with up to 2.8K LCD or OLED. Devices have up to six speakers with Dolby Atmos surround sound and “studio-quality, background noise-canceling” microphones.

Googlebooks are made from “premium materials” like aluminum, magnesium, or carbon fiber.

There are also backlit keyboards and large glass trackpads with haptic feedback and support for gestures. Google touts up to 14 hours of video playback and 16 hours of web browsing.

Finally, all devices have a Glowbar on the cover that lights up in the Google colors when you open and close the lid. When you plug in a charger, there’s a current charge level indicator and “playful” animation when you talk to Gemini. Notably (unlike Pixel Glow), third-party apps can access it to “build custom, interactive animations.”

title: Apple releases Xcode 27.1 beta, enabling iPhone Duo app development
snippet: Apple has released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 for developers. This version specifically enables app development that targets the new foldable iPhone Duo. more…
fullText:
Apple has released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 for developers. This version specifically enables app development that targets the new foldable iPhone Duo.

While iPhone Duo doesn’t launch until October, today’s Xcode release gives developers a chance to prepare for initial iPhone Duo support. 

Properly optimizing most apps for iPhone Duo will probably take more than a few weeks for most apps. However, Xcode 27.1 meets Apple’s promise to release dev tools before the end of September.

Apps built against Apple’s iOS 26 SDK will need to be updated for iOS 27 for basic iPhone Duo support.

Apps made for iOS 27.1 and later will take full advantage of the larger display. Still, there are a lot of sizing and layout considerations that developers need to consider when shipping proper app support.

While the device isn’t out yet, Xcode 27.1 beta also gives developers the chance to virtually experience their apps on the iPhone Duo simulator.

Xcode 27.1 beta is available to download from Apple’s developer webpage here.

The release follows the introduction of Xcode 27.2 beta earlier this week. Apple is shipping iOS 27.2 as the next software update for iPhones running iOS 27.0 with the exception of the iPhone Duo.

 It will run iOS 27.1, a version designed for the foldable device, before syncing up with the rest of the iPhone lineup in a later version.

iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order on October 16 and ships October 23. Pricing starts at $1999.

title: New Mac mini drops support for aftermarket storage upgrades
snippet: When Apple released the M4 Mac mini two years ago, teardowns quickly revealed a pleasant surprise: the internal SSD was not soldered to the logic board. This allowed for aftermarket storage upgrades, and we even showed you how to do it. With the new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini updates, however, it appears the storage is soldered to the logic board once again. more…
fullText:
When Apple released the M4 Mac mini two years ago, teardowns quickly revealed a pleasant surprise: the internal SSD was not soldered to the logic board. This allowed for aftermarket storage upgrades, and we even showed you how to do it.

With the new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini updates, however, it appears the storage is soldered to the logic board once again.

New Mac mini takes a step backward with soldered storage

In a blog post, the folks at Expand Mac mini revealed that the NAND is soldered to the logic board, similar to the M1 and M2 versions of the Mac mini. This means the SSD module is no longer removable.

Expand Mac mini sells storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro versions of the Mac mini. As it stands right now, however, they say that “support for the M6 and M5 Pro now looks unlikely.”

No slot means nothing to swap, and very little room left for us. In August we said we would extend our coverage once we had tested real hardware. This is the result, and not the one we hoped for.

We will keep looking for an opening, but support for the M6 and M5 Pro now looks unlikely. If that changes, you will hear it here first.

For comparison’s sake, Expand Mac mini’s 1TB SSD expansion module for the M4 Mac mini costs $300. Apple charges $500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini’s 2TB module costs $420, while Apple charges $1,000 for the upgrade.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple’s repair guide still shows removable SSDs. We haven’t spotted any teardowns yet confirming that information.

While it’s not the same as upgrading the internal storage, Satechi makes a clever accessory that includes an SSD enclosure along with additional ports for the M6 Mac mini.

title: MediaTek’s flagship laptop chip is the Dimensity CX C10 Max, debuts in a Lenovo Googlebook
snippet: The initial batch of Googlebook laptops that debuted earlier today use either Intel or Qualcomm chipsets, but MediaTek has confirmed it will also be backing the platform with the debut of its flagship laptop chip, the Dimensity CX C10 Max, which will show up in an incoming Lenovo Googlebook. more…
fullText:
The initial batch of Googlebook laptops that debuted earlier today use either Intel or Qualcomm chipsets, but MediaTek has confirmed it will also be backing the platform with the debut of its flagship laptop chip, the Dimensity CX C10 Max, which will show up in an incoming Lenovo Googlebook.

Following Qualcomm’s push in recent years on the Snapdragon X lineup, MediaTek is introducing its CX line of “Compute Experiences” chips. The first release is the Dimensity CX C10 Max, a 3nm chip built on TSMC’s process with an octa-core All Big Core design – 1x Arm Cortex-X925, 3x Arm Cortex-X4, 4x Arm Cortex-A720 –, 11-core GPU, and a dedicated NPU for boosting AI performance – all without fans or battery woes.

MediaTek explains:

Built on TSMC’s advanced 3nm process, Dimensity CX C10 Max utilizes an All Big Core design with octa-core CPU, 11-core GPU, and MediaTek’s 8th-generation NPU in a highly efficient platform engineered to deliver stellar performance across multitasking, productivity, entertainment, intelligent assistance, and more. Its power-efficient architecture enables manufacturers to design thinner, lighter, and fanless devices with all-day battery life.

The C10 Max is said to deliver 55 TOPs of performance for AI tasks while also offering features such as Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 (though not in Googlebooks), and more.

	

MediaTek says in an email to 9to5Google that the Dimensity CX C10 Max will make its debut in an upcoming Googlebook product from Lenovo. That’s not the initial Lenovo Googlebook (15-inch) which is powered by Intel. Presumably, it’s for Lenovo’s leaked tablet that’s using the Googlebook OS.

title: Google confirms Pixel phones were exploited in ‘targeted’ attack related to modem
snippet: Google has confirmed that a “limited” number of Pixel phones were attacked by a vulnerability related to the modem on the device. more…
fullText:
Google has confirmed that a “limited” number of Pixel phones were attacked by a vulnerability related to the modem on the device.

As part of the September 2026 security update, Google patched over 200 security vulnerabilities, but specifically calls out that one of those was actively exploited in the wild.

Note: There are indications that CVE-2026-58704 may be under limited, targeted exploitation.

The issue is related to the modem, with a bypass that requires no user interaction. CVE-2026-58704 is described as follows:

In Cellular Modem, there is a possible permission bypass due to a logic error in the code. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

Exact details of how the vulnerability was exploited are unclear – as well as which models were affected – but CISA (via The Hacker News) says that it was exploited on Pixel phones, explaining that “Google Pixel devices contain an improper authorization vulnerability in the cellular modem.” Combined with Google’s announcement, this was used in the wild, apparently to hack “targeted” devices. CISA issued a notice that this is a “known exploited vulnerability,” explaining that “this type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.” TechCrunch notes that this is called a “zero-click” attack, adding that Google hadn’t replied to a request for comment around the vulnerability being exploited and who was exploiting it.

	

If you’re on a Pixel phone, updating to the September 2026 patch, rolling out now, fixes the issue.

title: watchOS 27.2 beta 2 brings the App Switcher back with a new gesture
snippet: If you’ve been missing the double-click of the Digital Crown that used to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch before watchOS 27, it looks like the feature is making a comeback as of watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
If you’ve been missing the double-click of the Digital Crown that used to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch before watchOS 27, it looks like the feature is making a comeback as of watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the details.

Apple working to bring watchOS App Switcher back

Earlier today, Apple rolled out watchOS 27.2 beta 2 for developers, less than a week after releasing beta 1.

Included in today’s beta is a tidbit that will likely please longtime Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 had removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.

In his piece, he noted that there was no longer any way to quickly jump between recent apps, and wished Apple would restore the gesture before releasing watchOS 27, or in a future update.

While Apple didn’t bring back the App Switcher’s Digital Crown shortcut in today’s watchOS 27.2 beta 2, it did restore the App Switcher itself with a new gesture.

As spotted by the Apple Den Discord server and shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 lets users press and hold the bottom of the screen while inside an app to bring up the App Switcher.

Apple has brought back the App Switcher!

On watchOS 26 and earlier, you could access the App Switcher by double-clicking the Digital Crown, then turning the Digital Crown to navigate through your recently used apps. You could also swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to… pic.twitter.com/G5fa0TeTR9

— 𝓑𝓸𝓷𝓮𝓼 (@limpless_skelly) September 22, 2026

As Bones noted in their tweet, the App Switcher otherwise works much like it did before: after activating the App Switcher with a long press on the bottom of the screen, users can turn the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the “X” button to remove it from the switcher.

While, like with any beta, there is no guarantee that this exact interaction will make it into the final release (likely to come next month), its addition in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 suggests that Apple is listening to user feedback and looking for a way to bring the App Switcher back.

Have you been missing the App Switcher on watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

title: Peloton is back with a ‘cheaper’ folding treadmill
snippet: Peloton said phones aren’t the only things that can fold. Last year, Peloton did a sweeping refresh of its hardware that added cameras, fans, and AI-powered software called Peloton IQ. This year, it's zeroing in on its treadmill lineup - refreshing its two existing Treads and adding the new, more affordable Tread Flex into the fold. At a New York City launch event, Peloton chief product officer Nick Caldwell told the press the $2,195 Flex - which can be folded upright to save 50 percent more floor space - was meant to address user feedback for a more easily stowed machine. When folded, the Flex purportedly has a smaller overall footprint than the Bike Plus. It also has caster wheels so it can be m … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Last year, Peloton did a sweeping refresh of its hardware that added cameras, fans, and AI-powered software called Peloton IQ. This year, it’s zeroing in on its treadmill lineup — refreshing its two existing Treads and adding the new, more affordable Tread Flex into the fold.

At a New York City launch event, Peloton chief product officer Nick Caldwell told the press the $2,195 Flex — which can be folded upright to save 50 percent more floor space — was meant to address user feedback for a more easily stowed machine. When folded, the Flex purportedly has a smaller overall footprint than the Bike Plus. It also has caster wheels so it can be maneuvered more easily. For safety, the wheels can be locked in place, it has the existing Tread Lock passcode, and it has a slow-opening mechanism using a two-cylinder release. In person, it took about 25 seconds for the deck to lower fully. You don’t have to do anything or push the deck, and there’s no ka-thunk — it just sort of gently falls. That said, Peloton confirmed at the event that there are no sensor-based safety features.

There’s a two-cylinder release system that takes about 25 seconds to fully lower the deck.

While running, the Flex has a relatively quiet motor at 70 decibels. It’s hard to gauge exactly how quiet it is in a demo space, but it was notably quieter than other treadmills I’ve run on. I don’t think most people will have an issue running on the Flex’s shorter deck, but it might be a concern if you have particularly long legs. Like Peloton’s other treadmills, it has a swivel screen so you can do other types of workouts, but no camera, precluding it from some of the new Peloton IQ features (more on that below).

Meanwhile, its existing two treadmills have been rebranded as the $3,495 Tread Vision and $6,695 Tread Plus Vision. (The former is a $200 price increase, while the latter is the same price.) Here, the upgrades are more refinements. The Vision has a new deck that’s got better cushioning, redesigned jump buttons that let you go up and down for speed / incline, plus a redesigned tray for holding tablets, phones, and water bottles. The Tread Plus Vision also has the new jump buttons, plus a new “sled” mode that may appeal to Hyrox or Crossfit athletes. Both still have a swivel screen and motion tracking cameras that enable some new treadmill-related Peloton IQ features.

As far as software goes, all the treadmills are getting personalized pace. After about 10 running workouts, you’ll get a recommended pace targets that automatically populate within a workout. They may adjust over time as fitness improves. Peloton is also launching a new feature called ReRun, which lets you upload outdoor run course data recorded in the Peloton app or from a smartwatch into the treadmill so you can “re-run” them. That includes automatic incline adjustments based on outdoor elevation on a route. Peloton is partnering with NYRR so that users can “re-run” segments of the New York City Marathon course. At the event, press were told that the company is exploring partnerships for other famous races as well.

For the camera-enabled treadmills, Peloton is adding a running analysis feature. There’s a one-time calibration and then afterward, the movement-tracking camera will run in the background of subsequent workouts. Based on steps, cadence, vertical oscillation, and stride length, users will get a running efficiency score and tips on how to improve their form.

1/9The Tread Plus Vision now has a sled and free mode that lets you have up to 300 pounds of resistance to mimic pushing exercises.

So far, Peloton’s big bet on refreshed hardware and AI hasn’t translated into earnings. At least, not with its existing user base. That may be why at the event, it seemed Peloton was keen to emphasize who it was hoping to reach with each treadmill. The Flex, for example, was repeatedly referred to as the ideal treadmill for walkers, hikers, and folks living in cramped New York City apartments. Its “cheaper” $2,195 price is also more in line with its bikes, though that’s relative considering you can buy other walking pads and treadmills for much less. On the other end of the spectrum, the Tread Plus Vision was described as the treadmill of choice for performance athletes. The Tread Vision was envisioned for multi-member households who might have people at varying fitness levels. (Various Peloton reps and instructors also pointed out the new redesigned tray as a great option for people who want an alternative to a walking pad — though it’s not possible to hook your laptop up to the display as a second monitor.)

Peloton has repeatedly identified the treadmill space as one it views as ripe for growth in earnings calls. Altogether, it’s clear that Peloton is hoping these new treadmills — but particularly the Flex — might attract new membership signups.

title: iOS 27.2 beta 2 reveals new details about unnanounced iPhone anti-snatching feature
snippet: Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple continues to work on a feature that automatically locks an iPhone when it detects that the device has been snatched from its owner’s hand. Here are the details.

Apple still working on iPhone anti-snatching feature

Earlier this year, 9to5Mac first reported that Apple was working on a new iPhone security feature that can automatically lock the device when it detects that it has been snatched from the user’s hand.

While Apple has yet to officially announce the feature, new references included in iOS 27.2 beta 2 show the company is still actively developing it.

According to new code seen today by 9to5Mac, the feature, which is called “AutoLock” internally, can use the following signals to determine whether an iPhone may have been taken from its owner:

A sharp acceleration consistent with the phone being snatched;

A paired Apple Watch remaining unreachable for a certain period;

Loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch;

Prolonged loss of network connectivity;

The device remaining unlocked beyond a certain interval.

Additionally, new references include safeguards meant to prevent false positives, such as successful biometric authentication, certain foreground app activities that could otherwise be mistaken for signs that the device has been taken, and a backoff mechanism that can temporarily suppress further automatic locks after repeated lock events.

The code also suggests AutoLock uses a voting system in which a potential theft signal can request a lock, while safeguards such as biometrics, familiar locations, or certain app activities can veto it.

These new details add to the references already present in the code, including a location-based safeguard similar to Stolen Device Protection that accounts for whether the iPhone is in a familiar place.

It is worth noting that the feature is still under development and is not currently enabled or available as a user-facing option in iOS 27.2 beta 2. Rather, Apple has enabled the underlying AutoLock service in the background, while keeping the component that actually locks the iPhone disabled, possibly as a way to test the underlying behavior without actually triggering automatic locks.

This means that, for now, the new references only provide a look at Apple’s progress in developing the feature. Whether or when it will ultimately launch remains up to Apple.

title: PDF Expert update adds handwriting recognition, expands Apple Pencil support, more
snippet: Readdle updated PDF Expert for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 this week, adding several new features, including searchable handwriting in 29 languages. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Readdle updated PDF Expert for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 this week, adding several new features, including searchable handwriting in 29 languages. Here are the details.

PDF Expert now indexes handwritten notes

Readdle’s classic PDF editor, PDF Expert, was updated this week with several features that leverage new possibilities introduced with iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.

Chief among them is a new Handwriting Recognition feature, which works both within individual PDFs and across the user’s entire library, including existing handwritten annotations and notes added in other apps.

PDF Expert now indexes these notes as regular text, making it easier to find something the user might remember jotting down but can’t quite recall where it was.

The company notes that Handwriting Recognition currently works with 29 languages, matching the language support offered by Apple’s new PKStrokeRecognizer API. Presumably, as Apple expands language support for the API, PDF Expert and its users will benefit as well.

Importantly, Handwriting Recognition and library-wide search are available to PDF Expert Premium users. Free users can still use the Text tool to write by hand and have their handwriting converted to typed text as they write.

Additionally, the update adds support for the Apple Pencil Pro’s squeeze gesture, which opens PDF Expert’s tool palette.

Here’s Readdle:

Users can switch between pens, markers, highlighters, shapes, stamps, signatures, and measurement tools. They can also adjust color, thickness, and opacity, access recent or favorite tools, switch to the eraser, or undo and redo an action.

The company notes that this feature requires an Apple Pencil Pro and a compatible iPad, and that users can enable it by selecting “Show Tool Palette” in Apple Pencil settings if the squeeze gesture is currently assigned to another action.

Finally, this week’s update also expands the Liquid Glass look across the app’s interface, “including the sidebar, document viewer and its toolbar, and Presentation mode,” Readdle notes. Users can now also access dedicated undo and redo buttons directly from the document view.

title: Googlebook hands-on: What makes a laptop, a laptop? [Video]
snippet: After a protracted wait, the first wave of Googlebooks is now official. Having spent a brief period testing, here’s what it’s like to use one. more…
fullText:
After a protracted wait, the first wave of Googlebooks is now official. Having spent a brief period testing, here’s what it’s like to use one.

I didn’t quite spend as much time with the software as my colleague Abner, so for a full set of impressions on these laptops running Googlebook OS, please read his extensive thoughts. This is a little more focused on the hardware side, with a sprinkle of software.

The good news right up top: My initial worries have almost completely been washed away, save a few minor complaints about two specific devices; there’s more here to like than I ever expected. Notice I said “almost” as there are still concerns in the back of my mind, but despite lots of, I guess, negativity surrounding and preceding this launch, the entire lineup of Googlebooks has exceeded my fairly low expectations.

For more video content, subscribe to 9to5Google on YouTube.

	

I do believe that this is largely due to my mixed experience with various Chromebooks across the entire price spectrum, combined with the ultimately lackluster or barebones “Desktop mode” that was added to Pixel devices over the past year.

This time, we have fewer SKUs to deal with, and of the five Googlebook devices, there appear to be fewer pinch points – save the pricing. These are not going to be cheap, with prices “starting at” $899 and, in most cases, are going to be more expensive. That is likely where a portion of you are going to stop reading and just dismiss these entirely. I can completely understand why.

Without glossing over or forgiving the frankly inflated asking price, I do believe this comes with one distinct benefit. There is less compromise in quality, which is something that worried me, given the mixed history of Chromebooks and the pitfalls of the cheapest model becoming the flag-bearer for the “default” experience.

I spent around 45 minutes prodding and poking the lineup, and there are two standouts.

Right off the bat, the Dell XPS and the HP Googlebook were the most impressive launch devices here. That said, each of the five laptops has its own merits.

ASUS’ Googlebook, Lenovo’s Googlebook 15, and Acer’s Googlebook 14 offer, in my opinion, are marginally lesser but still fairly decent takes on the first wave of hardware. The Lenovo in particular takes some design cues from previous Chromebooks and pairs with a bright HDR display. It was really easy to see despite lots of glare and jostling in the testing area.

I will state that I am personally not a fan of 2-in-1 laptops, but Googlebook OS, as it’s being styled, just turns the Acer model into arguably the best touchscreen laptop-tablet hybrid on the market. In fact, all of these laptops have excellent touchscreens that run at 120Hz. I was worried ahead of time that we’d get 60Hz screens, so it was very good to see a baseline of 120Hz.

Windows and ChromeOS have always struggled with touch inputs, while MacOS doesn’t allow for user interface control with your hands – or stylus. How many elite touchscreen experiences exist on a laptop? I wager until now, none. This is where Android, in my opinion, is being leveraged in the potentially best way possible. Swipes, taps, prods, it’s all just like using your phone or a tablet.

Just dipping back into a specific device in the lineup for a second, the matte display on the Acer Googlebook 14 was a great touch. It just eliminated glare almost entirely and reminded me of the recently released iPhone Duo. My only gripe was that it was covered in greasy fingerprints and smudges after a few minutes of usage.

Lenovo, ASUS, and Acer are utilizing Intel Core Ultra “Pantherlake” chips, while Dell and HP are going with the Snapdragon X Elite chipset. All come with at least 16GB of RAM for optimal performance. Some SKUs might offer up to 32GB of RAM, but my session made no mention of storage capacities, and there is no way to expand storage using external storage like a microSD card. There could be a really easy way to get people onside by offering these in future SKUs; for now, it’s business as usual.

More good news: The performance is excellent. Every Googlebook felt especially snappy. These are desktop-level chips running Android, which sort of is to be expected.

If anything, I was shocked at how responsive the experience was. It helps that each device has almost identical specifications. You can pick the laptop that suits your specific needs and still expect performance parity. Given my trepidation due to how Chromebooks have been treated by OEMs, this was very refreshing. It’s a good sign right at launch, but let’s hope Google holds more cards this time to almost force device makers to hit base specifications once cheaper models arrive.

The touchpads on all of the models are genuinely impressive. There’s some level of haptics, but MacBooks still reign supreme here. Every keyboard felt tight and responsive, and I liked stabbing away at the keys however briefly. None of the five models felt mushy or squishy under my fingers, and the layouts were instantly familiar to my battle-worn MacBook Pro battered fingertips. I didn’t have too long to test out the two unique keyboard G and odd Caps Lock keys, but they’ll no doubt take a while to get used to if you’re coming from Windows or Mac.

We saw ahead of launch that the lightbar is a key branding differentiator on the Googlebook. Sure, it looks nice, but it didn’t seem to do much beyond, well, look kind of cool. Google is planning on opening this LED strip up to developers in the coming months, so I’m sure we’ll get various takes on notifications, DND mode, and more that I probably haven’t thought of.

Something that I hope isn’t missed here is that the XPS Googlebook from Dell is the first such laptop from the company to come without Windows pre-installed. I think, given how mediocre the Dell Chromebook line was, this feels like a real statement of intent for a product line that is widely heralded as the best alternative to a MacBook. The company wouldn’t stake the XPS line on a mediocre product. It’s a gorgeous small-form-factor laptop, and one I really hope to spend some extended time with soon.

Can Android fill in the gap Chromebooks leave behind?

There are so many question marks over the Googlebook lineup, most notably who the platform is going to suit best or how it’ll fit into someone’s existing computing lineup. Some will ship with HDMI ports; there’s no room for a single SD card slot, or at least one that I remember spotting. I’d love to know what the experience is like using a secondary display or taking that experience elsewhere.

I feel like the software is much better than I had anticipated for a launch product. Yes, we’re missing a few top-level professional tools, but the full desktop Chrome browser might dispel some pre-launch detractors. I installed an extension I use every day, and it wanted to track my cashback while I was visiting a few of my favorite online shopping haunts. That reduced some of my initial fears of mobile Chrome on a laptop form factor.

What I cannot fault is the launch hardware. It is solid.

I went in with some preconceptions likely based on some of the leaks and, I’ll be honest, a mediocre unveil during the Android Show earlier this year. The devices have done a lot of the talking, which is an interesting prospect, as they already feel like a fluid expansion of Android into a new form factor.

Right now, I am likely not the target market. I need certain pieces of software, but ask yourself: do you have one key piece of software that is locking you into your current laptop or tablet? If that is the case, you probably were never looking at making a switch to a new desktop platform on launch day anyway.

My overriding early thought is that a Googlebook is an option for someone who has no allegiance to a desktop OS, but has a strong urge for their phone to expand into a bigger, more competent portable display. That might be a tiny portion of the market, but it could also be huge given that many people still use a phone for 95% of their day-to-day tasks. I don’t have a crystal ball or next week’s lottery numbers, but we have a new operating system to choose from, and I can’t be too negative about it. Any challengers to Windows, Mac, or Linux are good in my book. We just need things to start moving fast right out of the gate.

I think back to the early era of the smartphone. I imagined being able to take my phone, plug it into a screen, and have access to everything I need or use most. If that really worked, we’d all be using Samsung DeX, but we’re all still using separate laptops and desktops instead.

The modern smartphone is a hub for payments, photos, emails, entertainment, and the “right hand” of most people. Here’s what is different: The Googlebook takes your Android phone and turns it into a laptop. Whether you want it is ultimately up to you.

snippet: The major class action lawsuit against Apple over Siri and Apple Intelligence delays continues to progress. Apple is expected to pay $250 million to settle the lawsuit, and you can now submit your claim to get a chunk of that payout. Here’s how. more…
fullText:
The major class action lawsuit against Apple over Siri and Apple Intelligence delays continues to progress. Apple is expected to pay $250 million to settle the lawsuit, and you can now submit your claim to get a chunk of that payout. Here’s how.

How to claim your payout from Apple’s Siri settlement

Verita Global, the Settlement Administrator behind the case, has set up the website where you can submit claim information.

The eligible class includes people in the United States who purchased an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025. That covers the window between when Apple announced the first Apple Intelligence features at WWDC and when it officially delayed the “more personalized” version of Siri.

Apple is paying $250 million to settle the lawsuit, while also admitting no wrongdoing. Legal fees and lawyers will take a chunk of the settlement. For iPhone users, the payout is expected to be $25 per eligible device. That number, however, could vary. If more users than expected file a claim, it could be less. If fewer claims are filed, the maximum payout is $95 per eligible device.

On the settlement website, you’ll be asked to submit your contact information as well as the serial number of the qualifying iPhone. You can then choose whether you’d like to be paid by check, PayPal, Venmo, or ACH. The deadline to submit a claim is December 21, 2026. 

The settlement website explains (via MacRumors): 

The Settlement will provide a cash payment if you purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16, iPhone 16e, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, or iPhone 16 Pro Max that you purchased between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025 in the United States.

You must fill out and submit a complete and accurate Claim Form below by December 21, 2026. If your Claim Form is incomplete, contains false information, or is not submitted by the deadline, your claim will be rejected and you will waive all rights to receive a payment under this Settlement. The information you provide will be treated as confidential and used for the purpose of this Settlement only.

While the settlement website is now live, it will still be more than a year until payouts are sent. The final approval hearing for payouts is September 29, 2027, and payments will begin at least 60 days after that. 

Are you submitting a claim to get your $25? Do you think this is a fair settlement? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Samsung Gallery is adding Google Photos backup to replace OneDrive
snippet: New updates are starting to roll out that will let Samsung Gallery replace its OneDrive integration with Google Photos support. more…
fullText:
New updates are starting to roll out that will let Samsung Gallery replace its OneDrive integration with Google Photos support.

Earlier this year, Samsung Gallery removed integration with OneDrive and, in turn, also removed native cloud backup for Galaxy users. Users could, of course, use apps from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, or any other number of providers, but there was nothing built into Samsung’s own Gallery app anymore.

Now, Samsung is confirming its replacement.

In an update to the “Gallery Cloud Sync” app on Samsung devices, the company says:

	

Gallery Cloud Sync is a service that safely backs up your precious memories to Google Cloud, allowing you to enjoy them seamlessly on all your devices at any time. View photos taken on your smartphone right away on your tablet.

Easy and secure backup: Safely store your Gallery photos, videos, and albums in the Cloud.

Seamless multi-device sync: No matter which device you use, your Gallery is always kept identical and up to date.

Google Cloud-based reliability: Provides a fast and stable environment through Google’s trusted cloud storage.

Edited for formatting

The mention of “Google Cloud” here is a bit misleading, as Samsung Gallery is adopting direct Google Photos integration, as shown by an early preview of this functionality by @WigettaGaming and SammyGuru writer “That Josh Guy” on Twitter/X. It’s not live just yet – at least in our testing – but Samsung Gallery will offer support for “Sync with Google,” including the ability to see available storage via the Gallery app, choosing which albums to sync, and what data conditions must be met to sync.

Samsung requires the “Gallery Cloud Sync” app and “Samsung Cloud” to both be updated, but it seems a Gallery app update or perhaps even a full system update will be required to get this working fully.

Google Photos integration like this has existed for a few years now, previously being added to the OnePlus Gallery app in 2024 and on devices from Xiaomi and select other brands. Google’s support page on the topic does not yet mention Samsung.

Samsung Gallery will still let existing OneDrive users sync their photos through September 30, but it’s great to see a replacement lined up.

title: Android Canary 2609 adds ‘Require unlock for Quick Settings’ on Pixel
snippet: Google today is rolling out Android Canary 2609 with another update to Quick Settings that lets you require an unlock before making changes. more…
fullText:
Google today is rolling out Android Canary 2609 with another update to Quick Settings that lets you require an unlock before making changes.

ZP11.260821.010 with the September 2026 security patch is available for the Pixel 10a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 8a, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7, Pixel 6a, Pixel Fold, and Pixel Tablet.

Google notes that “support for Pixel 11 devices will be added with the next Canary release. Additionally, Google has dropped support for the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro.

As always, “Canary builds are highly experimental and are NOT recommended for general use.”

	

Require unlock for Quick Settings

Go to Settings > Display & touch > Lock screen for the new “Require unlock for Quick Settings” toggle that is off by default: “To prevent unauthorized changes, you must unlock your device to use Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile Data, and Airplane Mode.”

When enabled, you can still open the Quick Settings panel from the lockscreen, but tapping on those key Tiles will prompt you to fingerprint or PIN unlock. The flashlight, rotation, dark theme, etc. don’t require authorization.

Audio streams Quick Settings Tile

Additionally, the “Voice broadcast” Tile moves from system apps to Connectivity.

Notification Intelligence 

Appearing on older devices (Pixel 8) with just the existing Notification cooldown feature.

title: Google goes in-depth, and a bit NSFW, on Noto 3D emoji as Android rollout expands
snippet: Google Design published a more detailed explanation of Noto 3D today as it expands beyond Pixel devices. more…
fullText:
Google Design published a more detailed explanation of Noto 3D today as it expands beyond Pixel devices.

Google explains that the design process for Noto 3D involved “drawing, sculpting, and debating every single character by hand so that dimension never came at the cost of soul.”

Noto 3D prioritizes “emotional clarity” over “treating emoji as miniature scans of the natural world.”

Our job was to preserve the vibe behind each symbol: using 3D to give the character a body, but illustration to give it a soul.

Research found that “highly anatomical details like irises or nostril depth actually slow down how fast our brains process emotion,” so the aim was to remove “extraneous detail and [keep] facial geometry minimal.” Additionally, “excessive props and texture destroy comprehension,” with “background features and accessories” becoming “visual static” at 18×18 pixels.

	

The design team ultimately decided that “every emoji gets at most three essential details to communicate what it is.”

In going from flat assets to three dimensions, Google asked: “What does the back of a smiley face look like?” NSFW (truly) joke aside, the team found examples like how the poodle emoji only had three legs.

Meanwhile, the same research found that “people empathize far more with complete silhouettes — especially when it comes to depicting real animals.” As such, Google moved away from floating heads. 

Seeing an animal’s stance, paws, and posture helps communicate intent. Upon learning this last year, we updated a few animal emoji, like the raccoon, to embrace its full mischievous self — and now in 3D.

Following the Pixel 11 launch, Noto 3D is now “rolling out across Google apps, Android, and select devices from partners including Nothing, Lenovo, Xiaomi, OPPO, OnePlus, realme, vivo, iQOO, HONOR, TECNO, Infinix, itel, [and] Motorola.” You can also browse the entire collection on Google’s dedicated page.

Throwing a smartphone chip, a power supply, some basic speakers, and a few ports in a small box shouldn' … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Antonio G. Di Benedetto

 

is a reviewer covering laptops and the occasional gadget. He spent over 15 years in the photography industry before joining The Verge as a deals writer in 2021.

The Mac Mini is a great little desktop computer, and back when it cost $599, it was easy to recommend to anyone who wanted something speedy, simple, and cheap. The new M6 model is even better, but it starts at $899, and its 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU might actually be overkill for someone who just wants macOS and mostly does web stuff.

That’s why we need a Mac Neo. The MacBook Neo proves Apple can get good-enough laptop performance from an iPhone chip for $699. And you get a great screen, keyboard, trackpad, and battery with that money. Throwing a smartphone chip, a power supply, some basic speakers, and a few ports in a small box shouldn’t cost all that much if a whole-ass laptop version is $699. I mean, it’s a screenless phone with a couple of USB ports, Michael. What could it cost? $499?

And while the current Mac Mini chassis is incredibly small for what it can accomplish, a stripped-down model with a phone chip and no fan could be even tinier. Apple could go super small or just repurpose something that exists, like the chassis it uses for the Apple TV 4K. Add some ports — maybe not quite enough, knowing Apple — give it a couple fun colors, and you’ve got a Mac Neo. Or, dare I say, a Mac Nano?

As Apple’s M-series chips keep getting more powerful and more expensive, there’s a segment of people it’s leaving behind. RAMageddon is making everything cost more, even the MacBook Neo, but the Neo showed that a lower-cost MacBook wasn’t just viable — it could be great. There’s no reason a Mac Neo can’t do the same.
