title: Android Auto update lets you customize your Google Maps ‘driving avatar’ via car display
snippet: Google is rolling out an update for Maps on Android Auto that gives users the ability to edit their “driving avatar” directly from the car’s display. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out an update for Maps on Android Auto that gives users the ability to edit their “driving avatar” directly from the car’s display.

The ability to change the classic blue arrow navigation icon in Google Maps itself is not new, but it’s only been available on car displays for about a year. In May 2025, Google Maps rolled out support for showing your chosen icon on Android Auto and CarPlay, but it needed to be set on the phone itself. 

Now, Google is rolling out an on-car picker for your Google Maps “driving avatar” on Android Auto.

The change is rather simple. Through Google Maps on Android Auto, a new “driving avatar” setting appears alongside settings for home/work and alerts. Tapping it gives you the option to pick your avatar and change it to the color of your choice. It’s the same functionality found on your phone, just now accessible directly via the car’s display.

	

This appears to be going live with a server-side update. Android Authority spotted the change with Android Auto 17.8.163744 and Google Maps 26.38.01.980791571 but, despite using those same versions, we’re not seeing the option just yet. Sound off in the comments below if you have it.

In our teardown of Android Auto 17.8, we also noticed that Google has removed the neat little “Jimothy” Easter egg which, as we predicted, was clearly never meant for a public-facing rollout.

title: Adobe Brings Its Premiere Video Editing Mobile App to Android
snippet: As more creators edit on the go, Adobe is making Premiere compatible with more devices, including foldables.
fullText:
Adobe is bringing its flagship video editing program to Android phone owners. The Android Premiere app is now available to download from the Google Play Store, the company announced on Tuesday.

Premiere is the mobile app version of Adobe’s flagship video editing software, Premiere Pro. It first became available on iOS last year, and now, Android phone owners will be able to edit their videos on the go, too. The app is designed to be compatible with all manner of Android phones, including foldables like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8. And as a nice perk for foldable fans, you can edit videos with the phone closed and opened up — the multitrack editing timeline and preview video are visible in each configuration.

Adobe has long been the industry standard for professional content editing software, from filmmakers to marketers and photojournalists. But over the past decade, as seemingly everyone has become a content creator, the company has faced increased competition from cheaper, more user-friendly services like Canva, CapCut and Instagram Edits. Premiere and the long-awaited Photoshop mobile apps are one way Adobe is trying to remain competitive.

	

			

As the demands on content creators keep rising, mobile apps are an increasingly popular way for creators to keep up. Some creators, particularly in India and Brazil, are adopting a mobile-only editing workflow, Diksha Kuhar, Adobe’s director of product marketing for Premiere, told me.

You can download the app for free from the Google Play Store. You don’t need an Adobe account or subscription, unless you want to use Adobe’s Firefly AI editing features or cloud storage, which may prompt you to sign up for a subscription.

The Android app was designed to work for aspiring creators and professionals. Beginners can scroll through the app’s library of templates and be guided through creating their own version. Popular tools such as enhance audio are available on the new mobile app, letting you clean up messy audio by enhancing speech and removing background noise. You can also directly publish your videos as YouTube Shorts from Premiere, like how you can directly publish Instagram Reels from Edits, thanks to a partnership between Adobe and YouTube.

In my experience using the Premiere iPhone app, I found it to be a relatively easy, quick way to edit videos. The auto-captioning is particularly useful. You can download videos free of watermarks, and there aren’t any ads clouding the app. (At least not for now. Never say never.) But don’t go in expecting the full bulk of Premiere Pro’s editing tools. If you need to do meticulous editing on longer videos, you’re probably still best off using Premiere Pro on a laptop or desktop.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Katelyn Chedraoui
						

						

							Reporter 2						
					

											

								

											Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators. Her work explores how new AI technology is infiltrating our lives, shaping the content we consume on social media and affecting the people behind the screens. She graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill with a degree in media and journalism. You can reach her at kchedraoui@cnet.com.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 missing one health-focused feature
snippet: Well, this is odd. The handwashing timer feature is currently absent from the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 hardware. more…
fullText:
Well, this is odd. The handwashing timer feature is currently absent from the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 hardware.

Handwashing detection and timer feature not currently supported by Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

Handwashing detection is still a feature in watchOS 27. It also remains a category in Apple Health, including the iOS 27.2 version. Handwashing detection works on Apple Watch Series 11 and Ultra 3, and it’s still included in the watchOS 27 guide.

However, Apple’s newest watches aren’t included in the supported hardware list. It’s unclear if that’s an omission or a hardware difference.

In theory, there’s no reason to even mention supported hardware if Apple planned to continue supporting the feature on its newest watches. 

Handwashing detection arrived in 2020 as part of watchOS 7. It’s likely this pandemic-era feature is just no longer supported by Apple’s 2026 hardware. Series 12 and Ultra 4 include the first overhauled processor for the first time in a few years. It features new Audio Intelligence features like Siri Recap and Live Rewind. Handwashing detection may have just been left out.

We’ll update our coverage if we learn more about the missing feature.

is a senior editor who has obsessed over headlines and internet speeds since 2011. He previously worked as an advocate for the National Park System.

Hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed on Monday after construction crews in New Jersey accidentally cut a Verizon fiber cable used for air traffic control.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said that a circuit failure led to the discovery of the severed fiber cable, ABC News reports. The outage hammered airports across the Northeast, causing ground stops at all three major New York City airports.

In a statement to CNBC, Verizon said that it bore “no responsibility for this incident,” putting the blame on “construction contractors working in the area” that “dug up and cut our cable.”

Ironically, it looks like trains make have taken out the planes, but fingers are still being pointed. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an Amtrak crew accidentally cut the line, but AP reports that Amtrak blames a New Jersey Transit crew for the disruption. “This incident occurred on New Jersey Transit property and involved a New Jersey Transit contractor,” an Amtrak spokesperson told NBC4.

As of Monday evening, Duffy said that “the telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming,” but cautioned that it will take “some time to clear all existing delays.” According to FlightAware, there were over 1,000 canceled flights today in the US

title: MagSafe Monday: BLAVOR’s solar power bank is built for fall camping trips
snippet: The weather is turning cooler, and it’s time for camping and football tailgates. BLAVOR’s 20000mAh Solar Power Bank is built for this time of year. It has four built-in cables so you can leave your bag at home, a solar panel for recharging, and a wireless pad on top for your iPhone and Apple Watch. Let’s take a look at it. more…
fullText:
The weather is turning cooler, and it’s time for camping and football tailgates. BLAVOR’s 20000mAh Solar Power Bank is built for this time of year. It has four built-in cables so you can leave your bag at home, a solar panel for recharging, and a wireless pad on top for your iPhone and Apple Watch. Let’s take a look at it.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Four built-in cables

This is what sold me on the concept overall. The unit has four cables built directly into the housing (two USB-C, one Lightning, one USB-A) plus three separate ports, so you can charge six devices at once without carrying a standalone cable, which makes packing a lot easier.

The USB-C port supports 20-watt fast charging, which BLAVOR says gets a typical iPhone to full in around 50 minutes (Pro vs Pro Max will obviously change). On the capacity side, 20000mAh works out to roughly 4 charges for an iPhone 17, 2.7 for an iPad mini, and 37 for an Apple Watch. Those are BLAVOR’s numbers, but the ballpark is right for a bank this size battery overall. A lot will depend on temperature, if you are using it while charging, etc.

Wireless charging, but no MagSafe

There’s a wireless charging area on top that works with both the iPhone and the Apple Watch, but it has no magnets. This is plain old-school Qi, not MagSafe or Qi2, so your iPhone sits on the surface rather than snapping to it. Set the bank down on a table, and your iPhone stays put. I won’t stay connected in a bag, etc Ideally in a future one, I’d love to see MagSAafe

BLAVOR only advertises the 20-watt figure for the wired USB-C port, so treat the wireless pad as a convenience charger, not your primary way to charge. If you want high speeds, use one of the four cables already attached to the battery.

Solar charging is a great addition, but it won’t let you charge the battery from empty to full. A panel this small cannot recharge a 20000mAh cell in a day of sun. What it can do is keep the bank from dying over a long trip and give you an emergency option when there’s no outlet nearby. I would think of it as more of a backup option.

BLAVOR packed seven extras with the battery: a flashlight with three modes, a camping light with three brightness levels, a compass, a thermometer, a carabiner, and actually rope. It’s rated IPX5, which means splash and rain-resistant.

Wrap up

This is not the battery you will use on the plane. This is a great option for camping, tailgating, etc. It’s a good, nice one with plenty of wired options and really handy for an emergency recharge via solar. Super unique concept, and it’s something I’ll keep in my camping bag, etc.

You can buy the BLAVOR Solar Power Bank from Amazon or directly from BLAVOR.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 introduce a new Theater Mode setting
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 include a new Health Sensing System that dramatically improves heart rate data. The new system also includes a new Theater Mode setting that you may want to enable. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 include a new Health Sensing System that dramatically improves heart rate data. The new system also includes a new Theater Mode setting that you may want to enable.

The new watches measure heart rate every five seconds, a big increase over the five-minute rate from prior models. 

As a result, the green light behind the watch is pretty much always flashing now. It’s not something you’ll notice when you’re wearing your watch tight. However, you may see the green light if your band is a bit loose.

For that reason, the new Apple Watches drop back to the five-minute interval in two modes: Theater Mode and Sleep Mode.

Sleep Mode dropping down to five-minute intervals makes sense for a few reasons. First, it helps extend battery life while you’re not active. Second, sleeping means the watch doesn’t need to detect physical activity in the same way.

Theater Mode is different. Toggled on and off from Control Center, Theater Mode is meant to prevent the watch display from lighting up.

By default, it also drops heart rate sensing from live to every five minutes. This is presumably to prevent the green light from being noticeable in a dark environment.

However, if you don’t think the light is visible and want the most detailed heart rate data, you can change a new Theater Mode setting.

In Settings > Heart on the watch, you can toggle on “In Theater Mode” under “Allow Continuous Measurements” to restore the more frequent measurements. 

For me, I’m not noticing the green light unless I intentionally peak under the watch, so I turned the toggle on for now.

If the option existed for Sleep Focus as well, I’d be happy to give it a shot and see how it affects battery life as well. The other option is to just not use the Sleep Focus, but then you give up wrist temperature collection and probably Readiness score compatibility.

title: M6 Mac mini review: Apple’s most versatile Mac continues to shine
snippet: Over the last several years, the Mac mini has become one of the most compelling Macs in Apple’s lineup. It combines impressive performance with a compact footprint, making it versatile enough for all kinds of workflows. I’ve spent the last week using the M6 Mac mini, and it pushes that formula even further. Here’s everything you need to know. Buy the M6 Mac mini: from $879.99 (Reg. $899) Buy the M5 Pro Mac mini: from $1,669.99 (Reg. $1,699) more…
fullText:
Over the last several years, the Mac mini has become one of the most compelling Macs in Apple’s lineup. It combines impressive performance with a compact footprint, making it versatile enough for all kinds of workflows.

I’ve spent the last week using the M6 Mac mini, and it pushes that formula even further. Here’s everything you need to know.

Buy the M6 Mac mini: from $879.99 (Reg. $899)

Buy the M5 Pro Mac mini: from $1,669.99 (Reg. $1,699)

Design

From the outside, the new Mac mini looks identical to its predecessor. Apple gave the Mac mini its first proper redesign in more than a decade in 2024, dramatically shrinking its footprint to just 5 by 5 inches. That same design persists today, and it’s still incredibly easy to love.

There’s something about having the small but powerful Mac mini on my desk that just makes me smile. The amount of power Apple has packed into this tiny footprint is nothing short of impressive.

It’s a delightful example of Apple’s design team at its best, without compromising performance or connectivity.

Connectivity

On the front, you’ll find two USB-C ports and a 3.5mm headphone jack. On the back of the M6 configuration, you’ll find three Thunderbolt 4 ports, while the M5 Pro version features three Thunderbolt 5 ports. There’s also an HDMI port on the back.

One nice change: 2.5Gb Ethernet is now standard on both the M6 and M5 Pro configurations. The M4 models started at gigabit Ethernet. 10Gb remains an optional upgrade.

The other two connectivity updates for the new Mac mini models include Wi-Fi 7 instead of Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 6 instead of Bluetooth 5.3.

For external displays, both versions of the Mac mini support up to three displays, but specifics vary based on the chip:

M4

M6

1 display

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240

2 displays

2× 6K/60 or 4K/144; or 8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240 + 5K/60

2× 6K/60 or 4K/165; or 8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240 + 5K/60

3 displays

2× 6K/60 or 4K/144 + 1× 5K/60

2× 6K/60 or 4K/165 + 1× 5K/60

Single TB port

Up to 2 displays

Up to 2 displays

DisplayPort

1.4

1.4

M4 Pro

M5 Pro

1 display

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240

2 displays

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240 + (6K/60 or 4K/144)

8K/60, 5K/120, or 4K/240 + (5K/120 or 4K/200)

3 displays

3× 6K/60 or 4K/144

3× 6K/60 or 4K/165

Single TB port

Up to 2 displays

Up to 3 displays

DisplayPort

2.1

2.1

Performance

My review unit is the M6 configuration of the Mac mini, so I’m going to focus on that for most of this review. The M5 Pro version is the same chip we’ve come to know and love since debuting in the MacBook Pro earlier this year.

Here are the specs of my review unit:

12-core CPU

12-core GPU

24GB unified memory

512GB storage

The M6 chip has two additional CPU cores compared to the M4 and M5 chips. It’s Apple’s first 2nm processor for the Mac. It’s also Apple’s first chip to use all three of its CPU core types: 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores.

The super cores prioritize maximum single-threaded performance, while performance cores are optimized for multithreaded workloads. The efficiency cores handle lighter background tasks.

Memory bandwidth has also increased significantly, from 120GB/s with the M4 to up to 170GB/s with the M6 (153GB/s on the 16GB configuration).

The M6 also features a new 12-core GPU, up from the 10-core GPU in the M4. Apple says graphics performance is up to 2x faster than the M4 Mac mini, including up to 2x faster ray-traced rendering in Blender. Each GPU core also includes a Neural Accelerator, helping the M6 deliver up to 4x faster AI performance than the M4 Mac mini.

I won’t pretend to regularly run local AI models or other on-device AI workflows, so I don’t have much real-world insight to offer here. But for people who do, Apple’s own testing suggests the gains are real.

Here’s Federico Viticci, whose AI opinion I trust, on the new Mac Studio: 

M5 Ultra Mac Studio Review: The Dream Mac for Local AI Agents

In Geekbench 7 testing, the M6 Mac mini scored 4,074 in single-core, 22,632 in multi-core, and 92,542 in the Metal GPU test. That puts it 24% ahead of the M4 in single-core performance, 48% ahead in multi-core performance, and 71% ahead in GPU performance.

Geekbench results, of course, aren’t necessarily indicative of real-world performance. Instead, they’re good for cross-reference comparisons to other Macs.

As you can see, the M6 also starts to encroach on M4 Pro territory, beating the 12-core M4 Pro in both single-core and multi-core performance, though the M4 Pro still has the edge in GPU performance.

Apple also says the M6 Mac mini offers up to 2x faster storage, and my benchmarking supports that. I consistently hit around 6,000-6,400 MB/s write speeds and 6,000-6,300 MB/s read speeds in Blackmagic Disk Speed Test. For comparison, 512GB M4 Mac mini configurations generally reached around 3,000 to 3,400 MB/s.

Pricing

When Apple debuted the redesigned Mac mini in 2024, we marveled at the price. It started at $599 with the M4 chip paired with 16GB of memory and 256GB of storage.

A lot has changed since then.

The Mac mini has become a go-to recommendation for people looking for dedicated machines to run AI agents and other AI workflows. We’ve entered what former Apple CEO Tim Cook has called a “100-year flood” in terms of memory prices, and there are no signs of that ending anytime soon.

In May, Apple stopped selling the 256GB storage configuration for the M4 Mac mini, making the base configuration 512GB. This raised the pricing floor from $599 to $799.

When Apple raised prices for most products over the summer, the 256GB Mac mini configuration returned, priced at $799 (up $200 compared to its launch price).

At the time, it was reasonable to think this was Apple insulating the Mac mini from any future increases (at least in the short term). Unfortunately, that wasn’t the case.

The M6 Mac mini starts at $899 for 256GB of storage and 16GB of memory. The M5 Pro configuration starts at $1,699, up $300 from the M4 Pro launch price and up $100 from the M4 Pro’s most recent price.

The thing that stands out to me, though, isn’t necessarily the $899 starting price. It’s that you still only get 256GB of storage. If the M6 Mac mini started with 512GB of storage, I don’t think there would be much room to complain about the price. Instead, upgrading to 512GB of storage costs an additional $200, pushing the price to $1,099.

So, the good news is the Mac mini is better than it’s ever been. The bad news is that it’s no longer the exceptional $599 value it was two years ago … it’s just a really good value instead.

9to5Mac’s Take

I love that we live in a world where the Mac mini is thriving. Apple’s smallest Mac, which has occasionally felt neglected, is having its well-deserved moment in the spotlight.

There’s a lot to love about the new Mac mini, including the faster performance and storage, all with the same great design. That combination of performance and design also makes it the most versatile Mac Apple sells, whether you’re using it as a desktop, an always-on server, a machine for running AI agents, or something else entirely.

Is it a little awkward that the Mac mini comes in M6 and M5 Pro configurations, as opposed to M6 and M6 Pro? On paper, sure, but practically I’m glad that Apple is focused on updating the Mac mini with whatever chips are ready at a given moment. That flexibility is one of the best things about the Apple Silicon era.

While the higher starting price changes the value equation, it doesn’t change my overall feelings about the Mac mini. It’s still an easy Mac to recommend for people who want a compact desktop Mac without spending substantially more for a Mac Studio.

title: iOS 27’s Wallet app adds feature that will make you want to use Apple Cash
snippet: Apple Wallet is better than ever in iOS 27 thanks to a handful of new features, including a clever solution for splitting bills with friends and family via Apple Cash. Here’s how it works. more…
fullText:
Apple Wallet is better than ever in iOS 27 thanks to a handful of new features, including a clever solution for splitting bills with friends and family via Apple Cash. Here’s how it works.

iOS 27 uses your iPhone’s camera and Apple Intelligence to make bill splitting seamless

Apple Cash has been part of iOS for years now, and I use it occasionally with a select few people in my life. But third-party services like Venmo and Zelle still tend to be preferred by most people I know for sending money.

In iOS 27 though, a new Apple Wallet bill splitting feature could make Apple Cash far more popular.

Here’s how the new bill splitting option works, per Apple:

With iOS 27, users can split bills using Apple Cash and Apple Intelligence, making it easy to settle up after meals with friends. Users can simply scan a receipt with their iPhone camera, or use a photo of a bill to split it with friends. This capability is available in Messages, in Apple Wallet, or by using Visual Intelligence onscreen and with the iPhone camera. For example, the new Siri mode in the Camera app lets users get information and take action on what’s in front of them. When users point their iPhone at a receipt using Siri mode, it can surface the relevant action to split a bill with Apple Cash and identify the items on the receipt. As users select their items, their total payment is calculated, including their share of tax and tip, so they can pay back exactly what they owe with Apple Cash.

The whole process is extremely simple and seamless. Just point your iPhone camera at a receipt, or choose an existing receipt photo, and Apple Intelligence does the work of identifying each item so you can mark what’s yours. It’s easy to add a tip too, with no math required as iOS 27 calculates common amounts like 18% and 20% automatically.

In my testing, bill splitting has proven an excellent addition to iOS 27 that delivers a very user-friendly experience. I love that it works from the standard Camera app in Siri mode, via the Messages app, and of course in Wallet directly.

The only real downside is that if you or your friends haven’t set up Apple Cash yet, that will be an extra step that slows you down. 

But once Apple Cash is set up, bill splitting is a great addition that I hope gains a lot of popularity over time because the experience is so seamless.

title: Samsung Gallery rolling out Google Photos sync, here are the details you need to know
snippet: As teased, Samsung Gallery is now rolling out support for Google Photos sync, though there are a few details worth noting. more…
fullText:
As teased, Samsung Gallery is now rolling out support for Google Photos sync, though there are a few details worth noting.

Through app updates earlier this week, Samsung confirmed it was replacing the Microsoft OneDrive backup integration in its Gallery app with Google Photos sync. The change wasn’t live at the time, but works similarly to integrations found in the pre-installed Gallery apps on other phones from other Android brands such as OnePlus and Xiaomi.

Now, it’s actually starting to roll out.

Following updates to the Gallery Sync and Samsung Cloud apps, a Samsung Gallery update is also now rolling out to some users, which enables Google Photos integration – we’re not yet seeing the update on our end. Ice Universe shared screenshots of the settings.

	

Samsung Gallery v15.9.01.7 seems to be the trigger for activating sync, despite other apps actually facilitating the sync.

On a support page, Google offers more details on how Samsung Gallery > Google Photos sync works. It requires your Samsung device to be running Android 13 or newer, doesn’t support Workspace accounts, and there are some restrictions on what media you can see and what features work.

Google says that images and videos synced from Samsung Gallery won’t work with Memories and highlights, Live albums, or Search in Google Photos. Samsung Gallery also won’t show content backed up directly through Photos – only content synced from Samsung Gallery via a Samsung device shows up in the app.

Samsung has access to the media items that were originally backed up from Gallery Cloud Sync, but not to other items in Google Photos that were not backed up from a synced Samsung device.

If your device has all of the needed updates, you’ll find the option to enable Google Photos sync in Samsung Gallery via Menu > Settings > Sync > Sync photos and videos.

Samsung Gallery’s integration with OneDrive ends on September 30 for those still using it.

title: Android Bench 2.0 focuses on long-horizon tasks, agent evaluations
snippet: Google’s development of Android Bench continues today with a version 2.0 that reflects how AI can handle more complex development tasks. more…
fullText:
Google’s development of Android Bench continues today with a version 2.0 that reflects how AI can handle more complex development tasks.

The first version “focused on incremental changes to existing repositories,” like bug fixes or smaller feature requests. Android Bench 2.0 targets “tasks of great complexity that take an engineer multiple days or even a week to complete,” such as adding new features, building apps from scratch, and converting cross-platform apps to Android.

This new focus required “more nuanced evaluation and scoring” that goes beyond pass or fail grading. Google is moving from binary to continuous scoring:

We calculate this completion rate through a combination of factors like functionality, visual fidelity, and avoiding regressions. We also apply objective scoring penalties for deviations from evaluation instructions or structural constraints.

Google has rated Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash, OpenAI GPT-6, Anthropic Fable 5.1, Kimi K3, and Qwen 3.8 Max. GPT-6 Astra is at the top of the benchmark with a 28% pass rate (compared to scores in the 90% range with the previous approach).

	

Google shared insights like how “porting cross-platform apps to Android remains an open challenge—no model hits a 100% pass rate, and frontier models reach at most a 80% completion rate.”

“…AI does a better job at writing new code rather than refactoring existing code. Refactors and migrations get trickier because success depends on architectural complexity rather than code volume.”

“Models show strong capabilities on well-established, deterministic transformations, such as converting Java to Kotlin, swapping Retrofit for Ktor, or introducing a ViewModel layer.”

“…models struggle when tasks require runtime validation (like missing dependency injection graphs), involve breaking framework changes, or run into knowledge gaps with unreleased libraries.”

With agent evaluations, Android Bench ran “agents from the corresponding model provider,” like Gemini 3.8 Flash on Google Antigravity and GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex. Google says “harness design positively impacts developer outcomes,” with Android Bench planning to include different model and agent combinations in the future.

title: Review: Satechi’s Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock pairs perfectly with the new M6 Mac mini
snippet: Apple just released a new Mac mini late last month, equipped with the new M6 and M5 Pro chips. If you’re looking for a perfect Thunderbolt 5 dock to pair with your new Mac mini (or your current M4/M4 Pro model) – Satechi has a great offering for you. more…
fullText:
Apple just released a new Mac mini late last month, equipped with the new M6 and M5 Pro chips. If you’re looking for a perfect Thunderbolt 5 dock to pair with your new Mac mini (or your current M4/M4 Pro model) – Satechi has a great offering for you.

Satechi’s Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock is shaped just like a Mac mini, making it a perfect companion, whether you have it side by side or stacked. It brings 8 additional ports, an M.2 NVMe SSD bay, and supports up to 140W of host charging if you’re pairing it with a laptop instead.

With Thunderbolt 5, there’s up to 120Gbps of throughput, allowing you to run up to three 6K@60Hz or 4K@144Hz displays with M5 Pro through a single cable, or two with any other chipset.

Beyond its display capabilities, it offers two 10Gbps USB-C ports and two 10Gbps USB-A ports, a 2.5G Ethernet port, an SD card reader, and a microSD card reader – with each supporting UHS-II. There’s also an additional 3.5mm combo audio jack if you need a second one.

The best part for me is the fact that it has an M.2 NVMe SSD bay, and the bay is large enough to fit SSDs that have a built-in heatsink – which can’t be said for every product with an SSD bay. The SSD bay sits within the enclosure and doesn’t expand the footprint. You can fit an 8TB SSD in it, at up to 6000MB/s – and it supports 2230, 2242, 2260, and 2280 drive sizes.

9to5Mac’s Take

If you want the best dock that can take advantage of Thunderbolt 5 capabilities and look right at home with your Mac mini, the Satechi CubeDock is undeniably the best option. I will say, it’s a bit pricey at $399.99, so it’s likely hard to justify for most people unless you’re super obsessed with running everything through one dock with an integrated SSD hub.

One thing of note is that it does get quite warm when you’re using it. It’s not to a concerning level, though you absolutely will notice it if you touch it. Is this an issue for something that sits on your desk? Probably not.

You can purchase the Satechi Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock for $399.99 on Amazon. Right now, there’s a promo where you can bundle an additional braided Thunderbolt 5 cable ($39.99) and unlock 10% off of your order, effectively making the second cable free with the purchase.

If you’re just interested in the new Mac mini, I’d also say they’re worth a purchase. They’re still readily available with delivery in September, compared to the previous M4 models which were incredibly hard to find:

title: Valve’s open-source ‘Lepton’ brings Android games to the $1,059 Steam Frame
snippet: Valve has just released its Lepton tool as an open-source resource for bringing Android-native games to Linux and, in turn, Steam. more…
fullText:
Valve has just released its Lepton tool as an open-source resource for bringing Android-native games to Linux and, in turn, Steam.

On GitLab, Valve has released Lepton as an open-source repository, allowing developers to use the tool primarily for porting games to the Steam Frame. Valve explains:

Lepton is a tool for use with the Steam client which allows games which are exclusive to Android to run on the Linux operating system. Most users should use Lepton provided by the Steam Client itself.

…Lepton is intended to help game developers bring their VR Android games to the Steam Frame. Other usecases are possible, but were not the focus of development and may lack polish.

The Verge points out that some developers are already using Lepton to port Meta Quest games (the Quest runs Android) to the Steam Frame.

The Steam Frame officially made its debut earlier this week, with the Snapdragon-powered VR headset coming in at a cost of $1,059. A waitlist is now open.

title: Google Home just became a power user’s paradise
snippet: Good morning. Today I’m finding some peace playing Lumines Remastered, deciding whether to get my kids one of the new 4th-gen Yoto players, and trying to figure out why everyone is freaking out about this recent Tom Cruise interview. more…
fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m finding some peace playing Lumines Remastered, deciding whether to get my kids one of the new 4th-gen Yoto players, and trying to figure out why everyone is freaking out about this recent Tom Cruise interview.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

Over the past few months, I’ve been using MCP (Model Context Protocol) to connect with my bank, my to-do app (TickTick), my personal database (Obsidian), and anything else I can get my hands on. I find it intuitive to have a conversation with a chatbot about stacking tasks, performing a complex set of calculations, or just figuring out the answer to a difficult problem. 

	

Now Google is getting in on the MCP action with Home MCP, a way to connect coding agents like Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes, and OpenClaw to Google’s Home ecosystem and the products connected to it.

Right now, the tool is limited to Google Home Premium Advanced subscribers in the US, but it’s an ambitious first step toward making it easier to interact with what is usually a digital rat’s nest of brands, categories, and compatibility layers. Google has already rolled out Gemini for Home in an attempt to make automation more straightforward, but I commend the company for dipping its toe into the DIY space and seeing what happens.

According to Google, MCP “gives your favorite AI agent real-world physical context—allowing it to analyze and answer questions about home activity, summarize camera footage across rooms, manage devices on your behalf, or even create your own smart home dashboards using everyday language.” I’m totally going to use it to teach my Nest Cam Outdoor that the cat who wanders onto my driveway every morning isn’t, in fact, a person. Wish me luck.

✉️ Inbox

Samsung Gallery is adding Google Photos backup to replace OneDrive. Good, no one uses OneDrive anyway.

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking powers Gemini Live, Gmail, & Keep. Google is the undisputed leader of text-to-speech, and Gemini 3.8 Live just extends its lead.

The new Boox e-ink devices get Android 16 out of the box, including Palma 3. The Palma 3 looks like an actual gadget, no longer a plastic toy like the previous ones, and I must have it.

Google confirms Pixel phones were exploited in ‘targeted’ attack related to modem. This is pretty concerning, especially because it was “zero-click,” but glad it’s been fixed.

🍎 Roll call

It’s iPhone review season, and because this seems like an “S” year, the camera is rightfully getting the most attention. That’s why I watched basically every second of all the new iPhone 18 Pro reviews from channels like PetaPixel, Tyler Stalman, The Verge, and Matti Haapoja.

I’m still not sure what to think about the aperture control. Most reviews are saying that it has very little real-world utility, while others are claiming that it was the only way to offer an f/1.48 lens without sacrificing depth control (or overly relying on software bokeh). Either way, once Apple decides to offer a hardware feature it tends to stick around whether or not it’s any good (see Camera Control), so we’ll likely see a few more generations of this tech.

Sticking with the iPhone theme, two of my favorite podcasters convened this week to discuss the iPhone Duo and how it fares next to the multitude of Android competitors. 

(And if you enjoy the conversation with Stephen Radochia and want to hear more from him, he and I host a little podcast called Old’s Cool that looks at new tech from a vintage point of view.)

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Tired of getting recorded against your will by other meeting attendees? Kalypta from Deveillance reportedly makes you “inaudible to AI” by “reshaping audio in real time” on your local machine. What a crazy world we live in.

OpenAI’s “Project Lily” tasks real humans with reading ChatGPT transcripts in order to make inference better and more accurate. According to 404 Media, which broke the story, “OpenAI is hiring hundreds of contractors who read a massive stream of real users’ ChatGPT prompts, with the prompts sometimes including sensitive personal information.” 

Snap finally let people try its $2,200 Specs smart glasses, a bulky and unwieldy computer that it’s inviting developers to test. The gadget has a 4-hour battery and can run real apps like Spotify while relying on a proactive AI assistant to do everything else. 

🤑 Action Items

Over the past couple of days, I’ve been trying out a new launcher on my Fold 8, a launcher unlike anything I’ve used on Android before. That’s because it’s defined by its adherence to the UX found on iOS — specifically the upcoming iPhone Duo.

From the demented mind of Reddit’s u/wolftech029, Folio is a love letter (for better or worse) to the way Apple’s home screen drastically differs from the ones found on various Android phones. From predefined grids to Apple’s App Library to the Duo’s funky blur effect, Folio has it all. 

I’m not sure it’s going to stay on my phone for long, but its existence (and the speed at which it was vibe-coded) is a testament to Android’s versatility and openness.

title: I Visited the Real-Life Silent Hill Village in Scotland
snippet: Silent Hill: Townfall’s setting of St. Amelia is based on a real place. I went to visit.
fullText:
I’ve played plenty of Silent Hill, so I know these games are full of unspeakable horrors lurching out of the impenetrable fog, desperate to drain whatever sanity I have left. So imagine my relief when I visited the real-life inspiration for the latest Silent Hill game and found it to be, well, utterly charming. Without a Pyramid Head in sight. 

Silent Hill: Townfall is the latest installment in the iconic survival horror franchise, and its creators, Scotland-based game developers Screen Burn, confirmed that the game’s fictional setting of St. Amelia is based largely on the quaint coastal village of St. Monans. St. Monans, as it happens, is about an hour’s drive from my home in Edinburgh, so I popped up there with my Leica camera in hand. 

During the day, St. Monans is a charming place to visit that’s often bustling with tourists.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

To be honest I’ve been to St. Monans many times. Why wouldn’t I? It’s a charming village with a couple of lovely cafes, an ice cream shop right on the waterfront and a plethora of old boats scattered around its ancient harbor walls that make for great photo fodder. I’ve taken hundreds of photos there over the years and made multiple videos about it for my YouTube channel. 

In many ways, it feels an odd choice as inspiration for the setting of a horror game. But having watched the trailer for the game, it’s clear that Screen Burn hasn’t exactly leaned into the picture-postcard vibes of the place. Instead of bucolic views and pretty flowers, St. Amelia is dark, cold-toned and draped in the dense fog that’s a hallmark of the series. 

The streets of St. Amelia, as seen in the game.Konami

The streets appear empty as the camera moves around, with shuttered shops and hand-drawn posters expressing the need to stay safe. CNET’s David Lumb had a preview of the game earlier this summer, saying “St. Amelia is small, but hauntingly empty. As you creep around, only the occasional ambient noise breaks the silence — creaks of signs, the sighs of buildings settling.”

The real St. Monans is nothing of the sort during the daytime. It’s a real, living community that’s often bustling with visitors on pleasant days. On my most recent visit, I sat and watched some fishermen tending to their nets while nearby a man on a ladder repainted a shop sign. It was all very twee, if I’m honest, made even more so by the daffodils in full bloom and the delightful blue sky overhead.

The architecture, the street lamps next to the low harbor wall, the pink-toned pebble-dashed walls. It’s spot on.Konami

But Screen Burn got a lot of things right, and as I walked around I immediately noticed a few angles that looked like they’d been lifted wholesale and digitized for the game world. The representation of the architecture, the various fishing paraphernalia scattered about, the shop facades — they’re all perfectly observed and recreated. 

A hand-drawn sign in a window in the real St. Monans.Andrew Lanxon/CNET
A hand-drawn sign in Silent Hill’s St. Amelia. Even the drainpipe is in the right place.Konami

The only thing missing for me was the fog. Scotland’s coast is often known for its fog (or the “haar,” as locals call it), but I visited on a glorious day that made it difficult to imagine the place as anything other than a tranquil haven. That is, until night fell. 

In the dark, things were different. The tourists were gone, leaving behind an eerie stillness, with silent streets that seemed to amplify my footsteps as I carefully trod around. The street lamps seemed to only cast small pools of light that quickly faded to blackness, making me want to hunt down these bright spots as though they offered some kind of safety against whatever Silent Hill terrors were out there.

At night, St. Monans takes on a different vibe.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

But my favorite element — and maybe it’s something that’ll make it to the game — is the telephone box on the harbor front. No, not your classic British red telephone box, but a more utilitarian glass-and-metal BT box that popped up all over Britain’s streets in the 80s. Casting its faint light from within against the gloom, it stood out to me as an incredibly Silent Hill-looking scene. It was then that I fully understood why this place was chosen as the inspiration for the game’s setting. 

Sure, St. Monans can be delightful, beautiful and twee. But even beautiful places, in the right circumstances, can transform into something more sinister, pulling the rug from under your feet as that imagined safety net is whisked away.

This phonebox looks like it was taken from Silent Hill, not the other way around.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

It took only nightfall for that to happen in the real-world St. Monans, and I can’t wait to see how much further the game takes it.

Silent Hill: Townfall is out this week on PlayStation 5 and Steam. 

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Andrew Lanxon
						

						

							Editor at Large; Lead Photographer, Europe						
					

											

								

											When he's not testing the latest phones or phone cameras, Andrew can normally be found with his own camera in hand or behind his drums or eating his stash of home-cooked food -- sometimes all at once.
															
						See full bio
excerpt:
I’ve played plenty of Silent Hill, so I know these games are full of unspeakable horrors lurching out of the impenetrable fog, desperate to drain whatever sanity I have left. So imagine my relief when I visited the real-life inspiration for the latest Silent Hill game and found it to be, well, utterly charming. Without a Pyramid Head in sight.

Silent Hill: Townfall is the latest installment in the iconic survival horror franchise, and its creators, Scotland-based game developers Screen Burn, confirmed that the game’s fictional setting of St. Amelia is based largely on the quaint coastal village of St. Monans. St. Monans, as it happens, is about an hour’s drive from my home in Edinburgh, so I popped up there with my Leica camera in hand.

title: iCloud storage notification glitch puts unremovable red badge on Settings app
snippet: There’s an annoying little iPhone notification glitch impacting some users on iOS 27. For those affected, the Settings app gets a red badge prompting an alert to ‘Activate iCloud Storage’. However, tapping on this alert simply navigates to the iCloud storage purchase screen and the alert does not go away after dismissing it. This glitched notification appears even when the user has plenty of available iCloud storage already, like if they are on a 2 TB family Apple One plan. more…
fullText:
There’s an annoying little iPhone notification glitch impacting some users on iOS 27. For those affected, the Settings app gets a red badge prompting an alert to ‘Activate iCloud Storage’. 

However, tapping on this alert simply navigates to the iCloud storage purchase screen and the alert does not go away after dismissing it. This glitched notification appears even when the user has plenty of available iCloud storage already, like if they are on a 2 TB family Apple One plan.

While Apple sometimes does use the Settings app as a way to promote offers (like Apple TV trials) and remind users about AppleCare warranties, this particular notification appears to simply be a mistake rather than some underhand way to shove an iCloud upsell in front of customers.

The notification appears on devices running the release version of iOS 27 and iOS 27.2, as well as iOS 26.7. 

Some users have reported that signing out of their Apple Account on their device and logging back in causes the alert to go away. But hopefully Apple can also resolve this quickly with a backend change.

Update: Apple Support recommends logging out and back into your Media & Purchases account on the device. Go to Settings -> [name] -> Media & Purchases -> Sign Out, then sign back in.

title: Is Disney Plus Allowing Ads on All Plans? Here’s What’s Really Happening
snippet: Reports have caused confusion about whether it’s the end of all ad-free streaming. (It’s not.)
fullText:
Disney Plus recently updated its subscriber agreement in Europe, and the change is causing confusion for customers worldwide, including in the US. Reports began circulating that the streaming service will allow ads to be inserted into content across all of its plans, leading some subscribers to believe that changes are coming to all ad-free subscriptions, everywhere.

Disney’s updated subscriber agreement doesn’t change the viewing experience for people who have a Disney Plus Standard or Premium plan in Europe. Subscribers in the US are not affected at all, and therefore, the current subscriber terms and ad-free streaming experience remain unchanged.

What you may see on all plans are ads, promos or sponsored content in live feeds on the platform and promotional trailers or clips may appear before or after playback in content for titles such as Disney-owned films and TV series. However, this was already part of the subscriber agreement, and it’s a practice that’s become standard on other ad-free streaming plans from Starz, Prime Video and HBO Max.

title: A Chrome bug is slowing extension load times to a snail’s pace on macOS, Google is aware
snippet: Google Chrome extensions are reportedly taking too long to load on macOS devices, when they should reasonably only take a couple of seconds, due to a bug in the latest updates. Google is aware of the issue. more…
fullText:
Google Chrome extensions are reportedly taking too long to load on macOS devices, when they should reasonably only take a couple of seconds, due to a bug in the latest updates. Google is aware of the issue.

The report comes courtesy of PiunikaWeb, which noted a thread entry on the Chromium issue tracker divulging the issue. The issue seems to affect macOS instances of Google Chrome, rather than Windows or mobile versions. The affected extensions are reportedly taking up to 60 seconds to load, when extensions should open instantly. 

Users began reporting extensions lag in Google Chrome last week, and one of the main third-party tools it seems to affect is password managers like 1Password. The credential management app offers an extremely handy Chrome extension for password autofill across any site that requires you to remember your reasonably complex password. According to the company, it’s aware that a Google Chrome update seems to be slowing extension performance.

Hey Don! There is a known issue in Google Chrome itself right now that can cause extension popups to take much longer than usual to open, and we’d like to figure out if that’s what you’re running into here.

When 1Password is slow or won’t open, do you notice the same thing with…

— 1Password (@1Password) September 16, 2026

It doesn’t seem to only affect 1Password. Some replies indicate other extensions are being affected by the bug, though it doesn’t appear to be consistent.

	

What seems to be causing this disparity in extension load times is mismanaged process priority on Google Chrome’s end, though that hasn’t been verified by Google. Specifically, this seems to happen on macOS 26, and for whatever reason, Google Chrome deems certain extensions a low-priority operation, effectively pushing them to the background while it diverts resources to other tasks. The result is a much longer load time for users.

Google is aware of the issue, posting a reply to the official community page. Here’s what Google’s team says:

We’re continuing to investigate this issue as a priority, and I’ve also asked the team to consider all options including if we can roll the experiment out any further. We’ll make sure to share further updates on this thread as we have them.

Some users have noted that, in the meantime, enabling the PMLoadingPageVoter flag fixes the issue. It’s worth noting that enabling/disabling flags in Google Chrome carries some risk, so please only do so with that in mind.

title: Apple Fitness+ team hit by layoffs, as ‘major changes’ reportedly loom
snippet: Apple is assessing the future of Apple Fitness+, according to a new Bloomberg report. The company has reportedly laid off a “handful of employees” working on the service, a move viewed as just the beginning of bigger changes still to come. more…
fullText:
Apple is assessing the future of Apple Fitness+, according to a new Bloomberg report. The company has reportedly laid off a “handful of employees” working on the service, a move viewed as just the beginning of bigger changes still to come.

In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman says the layoffs affect people working on the audio features for Fitness+. That includes features like the guided Time to Walk and Time to Run audio sessions. Gurman notes, however, that new releases aren’t going away “completely,” but rather they will “drop in frequency.”

Apple Fitness+, however, is not “on the chopping block,” at least as of right now:

I don’t believe, as of this second, that the service is on the chopping block, but given the considerable costs, ever-present demand for new content and subscriber churn rates, it’s an easy place for Apple to look to make cuts. And that is starting now.

These layoffs are likely just the first shoe to drop for the future of Fitness+, though:

Still, this is widely seen within the Fitness+ organization as the beginning of more drastic cost-cutting measures and other major changes to the service in the months and years ahead.

Last November, Gurman reported that the future of Apple Fitness+ was “under review.” Leadership of the service shifted to services boss Eddy Cue and health boss Sumbul Desai. Cue has reportedly pressed Apple to “move faster and be more competitive” in health and fitness.

Gurman speculates that Apple will eventually integrate Fitness+ into the revamped Health app. I think he’s spot on with this. What about you? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Report: Apple leads slowing true wireless stereo market as open-ear earbuds gain ground
snippet: Apple reportedly maintained its lead in the global true wireless stereo (TWS) market and saw modest year-over-year growth, even as overall shipments declined. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly maintained its lead in the global true wireless stereo (TWS) market and saw modest year-over-year growth, even as overall shipments declined. Here are the details.

Open wireless stereo shipments counter true wireless stereo slowdown

According to a new report from Omdia (via MacMagazine), Apple shipped 16.8 million TWS devices during the second quarter of 2026, a 1.2% increase from the same period in 2025.

Despite the modest growth, Apple still outperformed the broader market, which declined 0.7% year over year.

Apple’s shipments amounted to 20.5% of the total TWS market for the period, nearly doubling Xiaomi’s 10.4% share in second place. Samsung came in third at 6.7%, followed by Huawei at 6.2%, and OPPO at 5.0%.

Other than Apple, OPPO was the only top-five vendor to see shipment growth. The figure, which includes devices from OnePlus, rose 14.9% year over year.

Interestingly, Omdia also reported worldwide shipments of open wireless stereo (OWS) devices, a subset of TWS devices.

Essentially, Omdia separates conventional TWS products, including in-ear and semi-in-ear earbuds, from OWS devices such as clip-on and ear-hook models that leave the ear canal open.

Omdia says the OWS market saw shipments grow 12% for the period, with Shokz taking the lead at 1.1 million units shipped, representing a 10.3% market share and 107.9% year-over-year growth.

During its “Surprise and Shine” event earlier this month, Apple’s VP of Hardware Engineering, Dave Pakula, referred to the new AirPods 5 as the company’s “beloved open-ear fit,” adding moments later that “AirPods 5 deliver the industry’s best ANC in an open-ear design.” Still, it appears Omdia did not consider the non-Pro AirPods part of the OWS market.

Back to Omdia’s worldwide OWS shipments ranking, Sanag followed Shokz with a 7.6% share and 2.4% year-over-year growth, while Huawei came in third with a 7.0% share despite shipments declining 4.1%. Baseus ranked fourth with 6.6% share and 29.9% growth, followed by Edifier at 5.4% share and 0.2% growth.

Commenting on the results, Omdia said:

Omdia expects OWS to remain one of the most promising growth areas within TWS over the coming years. Annual OWS shipments are forecast to increase from 43.9 million units in 2026 to 90.5 million units by 2030, representing nearly one in five TWS shipments.

title: Google Home app brings battery-efficient widget, reduces gray device tiles
snippet: Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates. more…
fullText:
Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates.

The Google Home widget has now been optimized to “pause background updates and polling whenever your phone’s screen is powered off, locked, or running a screensaver.” This helps save battery on your phone and connected cameras, while “ensuring your widgets refresh immediately the moment you unlock your phone.”

Meanwhile, Google has resolved an issue with device tiles for sensors, cameras, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. They could previously “appear grayed out after returning from device controller screens.” As such, you no longer have to reload the screen.

Other quality improvements include:

	

Smoother multi-account switching: If you have multiple accounts that you use with Google Home, switching between them is now more reliable with fewer “Home not found” errors and preference resets.

More reliable smart device setup: Addressed several setup and onboarding issues, including eliminating stalls during Wi-Fi pairing. This ensures a smoother, frustration-free onboarding journey when adding new smart devices to your home.

Smoother Google TV startup: Resolved a startup crash on Google TV devices, ensuring the Google Home experience launches reliably on your television.

More flexible in-app banners: Improved UI for triggering actions in announcement banners in the Google Home app.

Smoke alarm notifications: Rolling out improvements to smoke and carbon monoxide alarm notifications to show current device status in the Google Home app after an alarm has already been cleared.

On the camera front, there are three fixes:

Improved camera live stream tile reliability (Android): Resolved an issue where returning from the full-screen camera view back to the Favorites tab caused live stream tiles to temporarily turn black until manually scrolled. Live feeds now continue streaming seamlessly upon navigating back.

Smoother camera history scrolling across recording gaps (Android): Video timeline scrolling now smoothly scrolls past unrecorded or offline gaps without freezing.

Faster switching to live camera stream (iOS): Fixed an issue where tapping the “Live” button while watching recorded events failed to redirect smoothly into the live view, leaving playback paused.

Finally for September 16, 2026, Google has five Gemini for Home voice assistant updates:

Improved follow up question behavior: Minimized cases where Gemini asks unnecessary follow-up questions or ends conversations awkwardly.

Fixed TV streaming playback: Fixed an intermittent issue that prevented Gemini from launching TV streaming providers on smart displays.

Reduced Live Mode interruptions: Addressed an issue where some devices interrupted themselves during Live Mode.

Reduced Broadcast errors: Resolved an issue where there were error messages when attempting to broadcast. You can now more reliably broadcast across your whole Home.

Improved Playlist reliability: Fixed some issues where Gemini wasn’t able to identify and play personal playlists.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 might finally convince me to switch away from WHOOP
snippet: Earlier this year, I picked up a WHOOP for the very first time. As a longtime Apple Watch user I was looking forward to having a new way of tracking my health stats in a cleaner interface that the Apple Watch wasn’t offering. Now, with Apple Watch Series 12, I’m very convinced to switch back to the Apple Watch. Here’s why. more…
fullText:
Earlier this year, I picked up a WHOOP for the very first time. As a longtime Apple Watch user I was looking forward to having a new way of tracking my health stats in a cleaner interface that the Apple Watch wasn’t offering. Now, with Apple Watch Series 12, I’m very convinced to switch back to the Apple Watch. Here’s why.

First things first, it’s worth noting that the Apple Watch Series 12 isn’t the only factor. There’s also the new Apple Health app in iOS 27.

The new Apple Health app has a much better interface. It offers your stats in a much cleaner manner. It’s very easy to understand all the data, which for me was the main thing breaking the Apple Watch.

Apple Health isn’t the only reason why I didn’t use the Apple Watch, though. It was also the fact that the Apple Watch didn’t collect data as frequently as the WHOOP did. The Apple Watch Series 12 now collects your heart rate once every 5 seconds, compared to every 5 minutes on previous models. This is still less than the WHOOP’s every 1 second, but so long as you’re not an athlete, I think every 5 seconds is fine.

Series 12 also introduced the new Readiness app on the Apple Watch, which gives you a 1-to-10 health score based on your HRV and other factors. This is akin to the recovery score the WHOOP calculated, which is one of the things that I like tracking, because even though Apple Watch always offered a sleep score, it wasn’t always the most useful piece of data. If you slept for a long time, you’d generally get a high score, regardless of whether other sleep factors weren’t quite great.

Wrap up

Only time will tell whether or not Apple Watch Series 12 is actually a game changer for health. As someone who’s used the WHOOP for the past half a year or so, I’m definitely looking forward to potentially going all in on the Apple Watch again.

Even though I’ve been a WHOOP user, I never ditched my Apple Watch, purely because having a screen offers a lot of utility. I don’t want to always pull my phone out.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max’s battery is so big Apple had to add this new feature to iOS 27
snippet: The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers a huge jump in battery life, partly because the battery itself is physically larger. In a new support document published today, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max has such a big battery that it has additional shipping requirements. more…
fullText:
The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers a huge jump in battery life, partly because the battery itself is physically larger.

In a new support document published today, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max has such a big battery that it has additional shipping requirements.

iPhone 18 Pro Max: New battery feature

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max has a battery capacity over 20 watt-hours (Wh). As it turns out, most countries and regions have additional shipping requirements for products “with a single-cell battery over 20 Wh.”

To accommodate these requirements, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max uses an “innovative battery-firmware solution.” That firmware will limit the battery capacity of the device to below 20 Wh until it’s activated by the user:

To address these requirements, iPhone 18 Pro Max uses an innovative battery-firmware solution that limits battery capacity to below 20 Wh from the time it’s manufactured through its transport from the factory. When you activate your iPhone, the limit is removed and the battery’s full charging capacity is available.

The shipping requirements, however, also apply to other scenarios like shipping the iPhone 18 Pro Max for repair, trading it in, returning it, selling it, or gifting it to someone else.

For this, Apple has added a new “Prepare to Ship” feature in the Settings app. This will discharge your device’s battery below 20 Wh and set a charge limit to keep it below that threshold.

Your iPhone 18 Pro Max might need to discharge for Prepare to Ship to complete. While your iPhone battery discharges, it might become warmer than usual. This is expected. Your iPhone will cool down again when it’s ready to ship.

You can use your device as usual while your iPhone 18 Pro Max discharges. This might take only a few minutes, but if you start with a full charge, it can take up to a couple of hours. When the Prepare to Ship process is complete, the Settings app will display “Ready to Ship” with a red badge. If you erase your iPhone, you won’t be able to use it while the battery discharges.

The new option is in the Settings app. Open Settings, tap General, tap Transfer or Reset iPhone, then tap Prepare to Ship.

You can learn more in the full Apple support document.

title: Android 17 QPR1 changes some Pixel status bar icons
snippet: This month’s stable release of Android 17 QPR1 comes with some unexpected status bar icon changes on Pixel. more…
fullText:
This month’s stable release of Android 17 QPR1 comes with some unexpected status bar icon changes on Pixel.

The silent or mute icon goes from a crossed-out speaker to a bell.

This might be an accidental regression as Google switched from the bell to the speaker in Android 14. Notably, this change was not present during the Android 17 QPR1 Beta cycle and only went live with the stable OTA this week.

Another icon change further complicates whether this tweak was intentional. The VPN icon is now much thicker and filled in, with this update also only appearing with the stable release.

We’ll know this was a mistake if Google changes it back in future releases, though any fix may not arrive until the sizable QPR2 update in December. Android 17 QPR1 is not yet available for the Pixel 11 series.

title: Judge rejects OpenAI’s bid to see X’s confidential settlement with Apple in antitrust lawsuit
snippet: Judge Mark Pittman today rejected OpenAI’s request to obtain X and SpaceXAI’s confidential settlement agreement with Apple in their ongoing antitrust case. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Judge Mark Pittman today rejected OpenAI’s request to obtain X and SpaceXAI’s confidential settlement agreement with Apple in their ongoing antitrust case. Here are the details.

Judge says terms aren’t relevant to the remaining case against OpenAI

A few days ago, X and SpaceXAI informed the federal court overseeing their antitrust lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI that, after reaching an agreement with Apple, they would move to dismiss their claims against the iPhone maker.

In the lawsuit, Elon Musk’s companies accused Apple and OpenAI of colluding to shut competing AI apps out of the market, including by preventing them from gaining visibility on the App Store, allegations both companies denied.

After X and SpaceXAI informed the court of the agreement, OpenAI filed an emergency motion asking the judge to compel them to produce its terms, arguing that they could contain information relevant to its defense as the lawsuit continues solely against OpenAI.

Judge Pittman then ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit the agreement privately to the court so he could assess whether it contained information relevant to the remaining case against OpenAI.

Today, he issued his decision, saying that after reviewing the agreement, he found that it does “not present information relevant to the issues” at hand.

From the decision:

The Court hesitates to compel the production of confidential settlement agreements entered by parties. […] Courts have, at times, permitted the production of confidential settlement agreements to the extent they contain information relevant to specific issues at summary judgment or trial. Having conducted an in camera review of the requested materials, however, the Court finds that they do not present information relevant to the issues to be decided at summary judgment or trial in this case.

In his decision, Judge Pittman also notes that OpenAI plans to file a motion for summary judgment (meaning it will ask the court to rule on the case or some of its claims without a trial), and that the court has granted the company additional time to prepare it.

snippet: MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process. more…
fullText:
MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro has a 2+3+3 All Big Core CPU design using Arm’s new C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three more C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz. Altogether, MediaTek says that its latest design delivers 17% better single-core performance and 15% higher multi-core performance compared to last year’s chip. 

Leading where others follow, the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 is a first-wave 2nm smartphone chip design that’s built to simultaneously raise the bar on performance, capability, and power-efficiency…

At its heart is MediaTek’s 4th-generation All Big Core CPU: a revolutionary 2+3+3 design pairing two Arm C2-Ultra processors, three Arm C2-Pro processors with 1MB L2 cache and three Arm C2-Pro with 512KB L2 cache, which altogether contribute to a 21% larger L2 cache system.

…MediaTek leads the industry with first-wave support for both UFS 5.0, which delivers 2x faster read/writes than the previous generation, and LPDDR6, which boosts effective memory bandwidth by 33% at the same frequency.

This latest chip adopts LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage. The G2-Ultra NX GPU brings a 27% boost to peak performance while hitting 24% lower power consumption. Ray-tracing is 18% faster and games support up to 185fps. 

On the AI side, Dimensity 9600 Pro’s second-gen Super Efficient NPU reduces power consumption by 40% while delivering better performance and higher token generation per watt. 

	

Rounding things out, the Imagiq 1290 ISP supports 4K240 native direct-output ultra-slow-motion video, 4K120 cinematic log, and AI-powered True Color Tone and 60fps motion capture features. 

One of the first devices powered by the Dimensity 9600 Pro will be Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, due to be announced next week. Meanwhile, MediaTek is also announcing the Dimensity 9600M as a lower-cost version of this chip with “flagship-level performance.” It lacks UFS 5.0 and uses Arm’s C1 cores instead of C2.

title: Android Auto update might fix cellular signal icon – is it back for you?
snippet: For months now, there have been reports of Android Auto’s status bar having a broken icon for cellular signal, but the latest updates seem to finally put an end to the debacle. more…
fullText:
For months now, there have been reports of Android Auto’s status bar having a broken icon for cellular signal, but the latest updates seem to finally put an end to the debacle.

The bottom/side bar on Android Auto shows your apps, the time, and your phone’s current battery and cellular signal status through icons. But, for around 4-5 months now, there have been reports of users seeing the cellular signal icon go missing at random, only to come back just as randomly for some. 

When it’s missing, it leaves a funny-looking gap in Android Auto.

Image via Reddit

With Android Auto 17.8, it seems Google may have finally addressed this problem more widely.

	

A number of users on Reddit all report that the latest update has suddenly fixed the cellular signal icon on Android Auto. That said, reports are limited to just a handful of users, one of which cleared their app cache following the update’s installation.

So, we’ll open this one to you. Has your cellular signal icon returned on Android Auto? Sound off in the comments and let us know.

title: Google rolling out Android 17 QPR1 for Pixel
snippet: Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch. more…
fullText:
Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch.

There are a number of interface changes in Android 17 QPR1, starting with more blur effects across the system UI. The volume panel is where you’ll most likely notice the Dynamic Color-themed translucency, with the full bottom sheet also updated. The Power menu has also been refreshed and is joined by a background blur. This matches the updates that the widgets picker received in the initial Android 17 June release.

The system media player has a new Material 3 carousel-based interface when there are multiple apps. Instead of dots at the bottom, you now see a preview of other open applications, with your current card shrinking to make room.

When opening Quick Settings, you’ll notice a new bouncy animation, while there’s a new icon in the bottom-right corner for making edits.

	

The Mobile Data Tile has been updated with a “Don’t ask me again” toggle. There’s also a new QS Tile for “Keyboard” that lets you access the system switcher. The Screen recording tool now defaults to the last-used application.

When long-pressing on homescreen apps, the menu has been split into app Shortcuts and system Actions (like Bubble and Widgets).

Meanwhile, holding down on an empty homescreen spot reveals an updated fast wallpaper switcher that has more pronounced corner rounding, while the gaps between menu items have been removed. Other changes include:

There’s a new M3 Expressive Settings app icon that was first introduced on the Pixel Watch.

New animation when launching the camera from lockscreen with power button double-tap.

Health Connect on phones can now track distance and calories burned in addition to step count.

Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out starting today for the Pixel 6, Pixel 6 Pro, Pixel 6a, Pixel 7, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel Tablet, Pixel Fold, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10a, Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

Visit Settings > System > System update and click the “Check for update” button if the OTA hasn’t already appeared on your device. Android 17 QPR1 Beta 9 users will get a small update to this final release.

The Android Beta Program will remain open and continue testing QPRs and feature drops. 

To get the stable version, those running the Android 17 QPR1 Beta have to opt out first. Devices will not be wiped by the stable OTA once that becomes widely available.

title: Amazon fixes bug that caused problems with Fire TV app sideloading [U]
snippet: Fire TV hardware will be able to freely sideload apps again without issue after an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware. more…
fullText:
Fire TV hardware will be able to freely sideload apps again without issue after an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware.

Late last year, Amazon rolled out a series of software patches to its Fire TV hardware. On the surface, the Android update for the streaming devices contained the usual security patches and performance updates. It was later discovered that the update also seemed to disable sideloading on certain Fire TV devices, preventing third-party apps from being installed if they didn’t come from certified app stores.

Amazon recently commented on that aspect of its previous Android updates in a response to AFTV News. Amazon says sideload prevention was due to a bug in the update and wasn’t an intentional part of the patch.

If users attempted to install a third-party app, the Fire TV device would list an error and block the process in some instances. It didn’t appear to affect all Fire TV devices, though the issue was widespread enough to be considered intentional. According to Amazon, it wasn’t.

	

There was a bug in a recent Fire TV Settings update that caused the “Install unknown apps” list to appear incomplete or empty on some Fire TV devices. We have identified the cause and a fix will roll out in an upcoming Fire TV Settings update, installed automatically on affected devices over the coming week.

This comes as the company recently announced its latest Fire TV Stick, which runs on Vega OS – not Android. It also confirmed that all future Fire TV Stick devices would run Linux-based software in lieu of Google’s OS to achieve a better performance-to-power ratio.

In essence, existing Fire TV devices will seemingly be able to sideload apps again, but that likely won’t be the case for streaming hardware Amazon launches in the future. Amazon says the patch will roll out to affected devices “over the coming week.”

title: YouTube’s login-breaking bug is getting a fix on TVs and consoles
snippet: Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix. more…
fullText:
Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix.

An issue began popping up for some users in the last couple of days, preventing a successful login on the TV or console app. Even with the proper password, some users were reporting they were unable to log back in after being kicked out. The issue seemed to persist on Xbox, PlayStation consoles, smart TVs, and streaming hardware – what YouTube classifies as “licing room devices.”

According to YouTube, the login bug that logged users out and blocked them from re-entry has been fixed. YouTube says the issue has been investigated and is now “fully fixed” in a community post separate from existing threads.

It’s unclear when this issue truly began, but there have been several new threads posted on Reddit within the last 24 hours, suggesting the bug affected a wide number of users worldwide.

	

The community post didn’t suggest an app update was needed. It was likely a server-side bug blocking Google Accounts from access, and in some cases, guest accounts.

Did YouTube block you from logging in? Is it fixed for you now?
